findings.title: slowapi keys decorated limits on the CONCRETE request path, so rotating a path parameter fully bypasses the limit on 7 routes
findings.evidence: Limiter(...) at rate_limiter.py:125-129 passes no key_style, so slowapi defaults to 'url': _check_request_limit sets `_endpoint_key = request["path"]` and __evaluate_limits uses `limit_scope = lim.scope or endpoint`. MEASURED with the real imported limiter: 25 GETs to /api/v1/comparisons/<same id> -> 20x200 + 5x429; 25 GETs to 25 DISTINCT ids -> 25x200, 0x429.
findings.repro: PYTHONPATH=<repo> python scratchpad/h1.py — mounts /api/v1/comparisons/{comparison_id} with the REAL `from app.middleware.rate_limiter import limiter` and @limiter.limit('20/minute'), then hits 25 same-id vs 25 distinct-id URLs via starlette TestClient. Output line A: 'same-id 25 hits -> 200s=20 429s=5' / 'distinct-id 25 hits -> 200s=25 429s=0'.
findings.impact: 7 of the 61 decorated limits are per-(client-key, concrete-URL) rather than per-route, i.e. no limit at all against a caller that varies the parameter: GET/DELETE /api/v1/comparisons/{comparison_id} (history_routes.py:139/170, 20/min), POST /api/v1/share/{comparison_id} (share_routes.py:21, 10/min), GET /api/v1/share/{token} (share_routes.py:53, 30/min), GET /api/v1/referrals/invite/{share_token} (referral_routes.py:257, 20/min), POST /api/v1/referrals/invite/{share_token}/quiz (referral_routes.py:289, 10/min), GET /api/v1/text/prices/{product} (text_routes.py:760, 20/min). Three are ANONYMOUS (share view, invite resolve, invite quiz, prices) and each does 1-N blocking Supabase/Upstash round-trips on the single event loop, so an unauthenticated caller can drive unbounded request rate at the one loop today. This also falsifies part of the M18 model: those 7 routes are NOT 'one bucket deployment-wide', they are unbounded.
findings.fix: Pin the bucket to the ROUTE, not the URL. Cheapest correct change: build the Limiter with `key_style="endpoint"` (rate_limiter.py:125-129) so _endpoint_key becomes `<module>.<func>` — this is exactly the identifier the repo's own tests already assert on (`'app.api.history_routes.get_comparison' in limiter._route_limits`, tests/test_rate_limiting_complete.py:76), so the two representations stop drifting. Verify at the PINNED slowapi 0.1.10 before shipping (local is 0.1.9). If key_style must stay 'url', pass an explicit `scope=` to each of the 7 decorators instead (e.g. @limiter.limit('20/minute', ...) with a constant scope string). This is a pure-code change with no flag, but land it AFTER LS-RATELIMIT-KEY-02's metering, because tightening these buckets while the anchor is still the shared edge IP converts an unbounded route into a deployment-wide one.
findings.test_first: In tests/test_rate_limiting_complete.py add `test_share_view_limit_is_per_route_not_per_token`: loop 35 GETs to /api/v1/share/<a DIFFERENT valid-pattern token each iteration> and assert a 429 appears. Today it is 35x200 and the sibling test (:90-96, same token every time) passes — that asymmetry is the whole defect.
findings.dedupe: new

findings.title: GET /text/prices/{product} is unauthenticated, unmetered, and its 20/min bucket is per product string — an unbounded paid 6-region price fan-out
findings.evidence: text_routes.py:759-765: `@router.get("/prices/{product}")` / `@limiter.limit("20/minute")` / `async def get_gcc_prices(request, product: str = Path(..., max_length=100), variant: ...)` — no Depends(get_current_user), no get_optional_user, no usage_service call. :790 `result = await get_regional_prices(brand, name, variant, search_query)` -> structured_comparison_service.py:8180-8182 `for region in GCC_REGIONS.keys(): tasks.append(service._get_price(...)); await asyncio.gather(*tasks)`.
findings.repro: Static + measured mechanism. The bypass mechanism is measured (see LS-RATELIMIT-KEY-01, experiment A: distinct path params -> 0x429). The cost path is read at HEAD: _get_price (structured_comparison_service.py:5587) builds a size-aware cache key from brand/name/variant/region (:5620) and only returns early on a cache/L2 hit, so a rotated product string misses cache and enters the tier cascade. NOT executed against prod (HARD RULE 1: no bursts, no paid-provider calls).
findings.impact: One unauthenticated GET per rotated product string = 6 parallel _get_price fan-outs, each of which misses cache, misses the L2 DB, and enters the paid tier cascade (Bright Data ENABLE_BRIGHTDATA_FALLBACK=true, Scrape.do ENABLE_SCRAPEDO=true, Firecrawl ENABLE_FIRECRAWL=true per baseline/railway-web-vars.txt) plus curl fetches on the 40-thread executor and Upstash/Supabase reads on the single loop. Rate is unbounded because the 20/min bucket is per concrete /prices/<string>. Today's Serper spend is gated by SERPER_LIFETIME_LIMIT=0, but the Bright Data / Scrape.do / Firecrawl legs are NOT gated, and the event-loop + thread-pool amplification is unconditional — this is the single largest hole in the 'mis-keyed limiter accidentally guards the loop' premise the M18 ordering rule rests on.
findings.fix: Three things, in this order, and none needs a flag: (1) put the route behind the same optional-user + usage metering the compare routes use (get_optional_user + check/record usage as at text_routes.py:154), or gate it behind verify_admin_key like its undecorated neighbours DELETE /text/cache (:863) and GET /text/parse (:898) if it has no product consumer — grep the app for a caller first; (2) apply LS-RATELIMIT-KEY-01's key_style/scope fix so 20/min actually means 20/min for this route; (3) bound the fan-out (it gathers ALL GCC_REGIONS unconditionally with no per-request region cap, cf. #70/#73). If the route has no shipped consumer, deleting it is strictly better than fixing it.
findings.test_first: tests/test_rate_limiting_complete.py: `test_prices_rate_limit_survives_product_rotation` — 25 GETs to /api/v1/text/prices/probe-{i} with _get_price patched to a stub, assert a 429 appears. Pair it with `test_prices_requires_auth_or_admin` asserting 401/403 for an anonymous caller. Note the ONLY existing enforcement test for this route (:31-48) is marked @pytest.mark.live_unit and is therefore deselected in CI, so this route currently has ZERO enforcement coverage on the green path.
findings.dedupe: new

findings.title: The limiter anchor is NOT one IP: production audit rows show 10 distinct Railway edge peers in 100.64.0.0/10, so the 'one bucket, ~5 concurrent compares' guard is ~N-fold looser than modelled
findings.evidence: Read-only SELECT over ALL 1439 admin_audit_log rows (the only store of `request.client.host`, written by audit_client_ip at rate_limiter.py:62-70 from auth_routes.py:437/465/488/506/644). ip_address distribution: NULL=719, 'testclient'=696, and 24 real peers — 100.64.0.3(7), .6(3), .24(3), .13(2), .28(2), .5(2), .4(2), .10(1), .22(1), .26(1). Every real value is in the Railway private/CGNAT range 100.64.0.0/10.
findings.repro: PYTHONPATH=<repo> python scratchpad/q2.py — load_dotenv('.env'); supabase.create_client(SUPABASE_URL, SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY); paged .table('admin_audit_log').select('ip_address,created_at').range(...) over all 1439 rows; Counter over ip_address. SELECT only, no writes.
findings.impact: Two corrections to the standing load model, both load-bearing. (1) The anchor is CONFIRMED as the Railway edge peer, and the exact CIDR to trust is now MEASURED: 100.64.0.0/10 — the #114 fix no longer needs to guess Railway's topology for the allow-list. (2) The number of buckets equals the number of distinct edge peers a burst lands on, and that is empirically >= 10, not 1. So 'every limit is ONE bucket deployment-wide' overstates the constraint by up to an order of magnitude: the aggregate compare ceiling is (paths x limit) x (distinct concurrent edge peers), and the ORDERING RULE's premise that the mis-keyed limiter bounds concurrent cold compares to ~5 is not safe to lean on. Conversely the DoS lever is undiminished: a caller sharing an edge peer with victims still denies them, and the caller cannot choose its peer, so this is a weaker guard AND an unfair, unattributable one.
findings.fix: Do not treat the current limiter as a capacity guard in any activation plan; state the ceiling as a range ((paths x limit) x [1..N_peers]) and get a real bound from the offload work (#71/#73) and a concurrency semaphore on the compare pipeline instead. Then use the measured 100.64.0.0/10 as the trusted-hop allow-list for the #114 fix. Before relying on the count, re-measure it after real traffic resumes: the 24 real rows are all from 2026-04/05 and are a lower bound (only 5 auth sites ever write an IP).
findings.test_first: No unit test pins a live topology fact. The pinning artifact is an assertion in the activation runbook plus a startup log line: log `client_host=<request.client.host> xff=<raw X-Forwarded-For>` once per N requests behind a DEBUG flag (see LS-RATELIMIT-KEY-09), then assert in the runbook that the observed client_host set is a subset of 100.64.0.0/10 before flipping any anchor flag.
findings.dedupe: known:M18 LS-ratelimit-01 + LS-railway-metrics-01 (both P1) — still-open, and REFINED by the first live measurement of the anchor; the 'ONE bucket' phrasing in both is wrong in the direction of over-constraint

findings.title: per_method=False merges GET/POST/DELETE on the same path into one bucket — /url/compare is 10/min for POST+GET combined, /comparisons/{id} is 20/min for GET+DELETE combined
findings.evidence: slowapi limit() defaults per_method=False (extension.py:783-792) and __evaluate_limits appends the method to the scope ONLY when per_method (:494). MEASURED: POST+GET /api/v1/url/compare interleaved 12x -> [200 x10, 429, 429]; GET+DELETE interleaved on one concrete /comparisons/<id> -> first 429 at request #21.
findings.repro: PYTHONPATH=<repo> python scratchpad/h1.py, output lines B and C ('B GET+DELETE interleaved on same path -> 200s=20 429s=4 first429=20', 'C POST+GET /url/compare interleaved 12 -> 200s=10 429s=2').
findings.impact: Changes the per-route capacity table that any activation plan is built from. Affected pairs at HEAD: POST/GET /api/v1/text/compare (text_routes.py:153/295) share ONE 10/min bucket, not two; POST/GET /api/v1/url/compare (url_routes.py:127/167) share one 10/min; POST/GET /api/v1/url/extract (:69/:106) share one 10/min; POST/GET /api/v1/url/detect (:190/:210) share one 20/min; GET/DELETE /api/v1/comparisons/{id} (history_routes.py:139/170) share one 20/min. The client's documented SSE-to-REST fallback therefore consumes from the SAME bucket as the primary call for the /text/compare path. Merging is conservative (it under-serves rather than over-serves) but it means the compare surface is 3 buckets, not 6, and a user's own retry costs them their next real attempt.
findings.fix: Decide it explicitly rather than inheriting it. If GET and POST of the same route are meant to be one budget (they are the same work), add a comment saying so at rate_limiter.py:125 and keep per_method=False. If DELETE /comparisons/{id} should not be able to consume the read budget, pass per_method=True on that decorator pair. Either way the number belongs in CLAUDE.md's capacity table, which currently implies one bucket per decorator.
findings.test_first: tests/test_rate_limiting_complete.py: `test_get_and_post_compare_share_one_bucket` — alternate POST and GET /api/v1/url/compare and assert the 429 arrives on the 11th combined call, not the 11th of each. That pins whichever semantics are chosen.
findings.dedupe: new

findings.title: referral_routes docstring claims the 20/min limit stops anonymous hammering — the limit is per share_token, so it does not
findings.evidence: referral_routes.py:270-272 (docstring of resolve_invite): 'M13-28: rate-limited (20/min) and both params are format-validated so an anonymous caller cannot hammer this or push arbitrary strings at PostgREST.' The route is GET /invite/{share_token} (:256) with @limiter.limit('20/minute') (:257), i.e. exactly the path-parameterised shape measured in LS-RATELIMIT-KEY-01 as unbounded across distinct parameters.
findings.repro: static — read referral_routes.py:256-281 at HEAD; the bypass mechanism is measured in LS-RATELIMIT-KEY-01 experiment A.
findings.impact: A security control's own documentation asserts a property the code does not have, on an ANONYMOUS route that calls ReferralService.resolve_invite (multiple Supabase reads on the single event loop). Anyone auditing this file — including the M13-28 closeout that wrote the line — reads 'protected' and moves on. This is the M13 theme 'docs-as-wrong-truth' recurring on the exact control it describes. The format validation half of the claim IS true (both params are pattern-constrained); only the rate-limit half is false.
findings.fix: Fix the code (LS-RATELIMIT-KEY-01) and then rewrite the sentence to say what the limit is keyed on, e.g. 'rate-limited 20/min per (client-key, route) — note the client-key is the shared Railway edge peer until #114 lands, so this is a deployment-wide budget, not per-caller.' Apply the same audit to the other anon parameterised route docstrings (share_routes.py:58 'No auth required.').
findings.test_first: Not a unit test — a docstring assertion cannot be pinned. The correct pin is LS-RATELIMIT-KEY-01's rotation test on this exact route: `test_invite_resolve_limit_survives_token_rotation` (25 GETs to /api/v1/referrals/invite/<distinct valid token>?ref=<valid> must produce a 429).
findings.dedupe: new

findings.title: The rate-limit test suite is green because every enforcement test hammers a CONSTANT path parameter; the one test that would matter is live_unit-deselected in CI
findings.evidence: tests/test_rate_limiting_complete.py:90-96 `test_share_view_rate_limited`: `for _ in range(35): resp = client.get("/api/v1/share/abcdefghijklmnopqrstuv")` — same token 35x. :31-48 `test_prices_endpoint_rate_limited` is decorated `@pytest.mark.live_unit` (deselected by the free-tier and CI marker filter). The other six 'has_rate_limit' tests only assert membership in `limiter._route_limits`, never enforcement.
findings.repro: cd <repo> && python -m pytest tests/test_rate_limiting_complete.py tests/test_m13_02_proxy_aware_ratelimit.py -m "not (live_unit or live_db or integration)" --timeout=60 -q  =>  '21 passed, 1 deselected' (local, off-lock: slowapi 0.1.9 vs lock 0.1.10).
findings.impact: 9 tests assert 'this endpoint is rate limited' and all 9 pass while 7 of the 61 limits are bypassable by varying one path segment. The registration-style tests (`'app.api.history_routes.get_comparison' in limiter._route_limits`) are especially misleading: they assert the endpoint-function key exists while the runtime buckets on the URL — the two representations have silently diverged and the test asserts the one that is not used. Green here has meant nothing about enforcement since the file was written; this is the M13 'green-that-means-nothing' theme on the security surface.
findings.fix: Add one rotation test per parameterised route (7 tests) asserting a 429 appears when the parameter varies; convert the six membership assertions into behavioural ones by hitting the route N+1 times; and un-live_unit the /text/prices test by patching `StructuredComparisonService._get_price` to a stub instead of letting it resolve a real price (the docstring at :42 already prescribes exactly this: 'Restore coverage by mocking `_get_price`, not by removing the marker'). Once LS-RATELIMIT-KEY-01 lands, the rotation tests go green and stay as the regression pin.
findings.test_first: `test_every_parameterised_limit_survives_rotation` — parametrise over the 7 (path-template, sample-params) pairs, hit each 2x its limit with a DIFFERENT parameter each call, assert 429. It fails on all 7 today.
findings.dedupe: new

findings.title: admin_audit_log — the only vantage that records the limiter anchor — is 98% junk: 719 NULL + 696 'testclient' rows, with the test suite writing into the PRODUCTION audit table
findings.evidence: SELECT over all 1439 rows of prod admin_audit_log: ip_address NULL=719, 'testclient'=696, real edge peers=24 (newest 2026-05). 'testclient' is starlette TestClient's client host, and rows carry user_id '00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001' with endpoint '/api/v1/auth/register' and details {'invite_code': 'QR-ABCDEF'} — synthetic test fixtures, dated through 2026-08-25. audit_client_ip is defined at rate_limiter.py:62-70 and called from auth_routes.py:437/465/488/506/644.
findings.repro: PYTHONPATH=<repo> python scratchpad/q2.py (SELECT-only paging over admin_audit_log; prints columns, samples and the full ip_address Counter). Sample row: {'event_type': 'invite_code_redeemed', 'user_id': '00000000-...-0001', 'ip_address': 'testclient', 'endpoint': '/api/v1/auth/register', 'created_at': '2026-08-25T14:01:05'}.
findings.impact: Three consequences. (1) #114 cannot be verified from stored data: there is no genuine client-IP series to inspect, so the hop topology has to be re-measured with new instrumentation (see LS-RATELIMIT-KEY-09). (2) M13-02's stated goal — 'every audit row records the same proxy IP so the abuse-investigation surface cannot attribute anything' — is worse than described: 50% of rows record a test harness and 50% record nothing. Any future abuse investigation over this table is unusable. (3) A test run holding the prod SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY is writing rows into a production security-audit table; that is a data-integrity problem independent of rate limiting (696 of 1439 rows, ~48%).
findings.fix: Two separable changes. (a) Stop the pollution: the credential-stripping conftest already exists for the free tier — extend it (or a CI guard) so any test that can reach `record_admin_audit`/Supabase with a service key fails loudly unless LIVE=1 AND the URL is not the prod project; then purge the 696 'testclient' rows in a one-off migration. (b) Make the anchor observable: have audit_client_ip also record the raw X-Forwarded-For alongside the peer (a new nullable `forwarded_for` column, or inside the existing `details` JSON) so the hop count becomes readable from data the app already writes, with no new endpoint and no live-egress requirement. Both are prerequisites for closing #114, not follow-ups.
findings.test_first: `test_audit_writes_are_blocked_without_live_flag` in tests/conftest-adjacent coverage: assert that calling the auth audit path under the free-tier fixture raises/no-ops rather than reaching a real client. Plus `test_audit_client_ip_records_raw_xff` asserting the recorded row carries both the peer and the unmodified X-Forwarded-For string.
findings.dedupe: new (M13-02 identified the shared-proxy-IP attribution defect; the test-harness pollution and the 719 NULLs are new and they are what blocks #114's verification)

findings.title: 429s carry no Retry-After and no X-RateLimit headers, and the client only branches on USAGE_LIMIT — a shared-bucket 429 reaches users as an unexplained generic failure
findings.evidence: Limiter(...) at rate_limiter.py:125-129 omits headers_enabled, whose slowapi default is False (verified by runtime introspection: `limiter._headers_enabled=False`). rate_limit_handler (error_handler.py:123-128) returns exactly {success, error:'Rate limit exceeded. Please try again later.', code:'RATE_LIMITED', request_id} with no headers. SmartCompareApp/src/services/api.ts:146-152 and :250-258 special-case status 429 ONLY when code=='USAGE_LIMIT'; RATE_LIMITED falls through to generic error handling.
findings.repro: static — read rate_limiter.py:125-129, error_handler.py:123-128, api.ts:138-155 and :242-262 at HEAD; headers_enabled=False confirmed by importing the real limiter and reading `_headers_enabled` (scratchpad/h1.py output line F).
findings.impact: This is the user-visible face of the shared-bucket defect. When another caller exhausts a global bucket, the victim gets an untyped failure with no retry hint: the client cannot back off (no Retry-After to read, and slowapi would supply one only with headers_enabled=True), cannot distinguish 'you hit your quota' (USAGE_LIMIT, which routes to the paywall) from 'the deployment is rate-limited' (RATE_LIMITED, which should say 'try again in N seconds'), and will happily retry immediately — amplifying the burst that caused the 429. It also blinds the operator: with no X-RateLimit-Remaining on the wire and no client IP in Railway HTTP logs, there is no signal that a bucket is saturating until users complain.
findings.fix: Set headers_enabled=True on the Limiter (rate_limiter.py:125-129) so every response carries X-RateLimit-Limit/Remaining/Reset and 429s carry Retry-After, and propagate Retry-After through rate_limit_handler (error_handler.py:123-128, which currently drops all headers). Then add a RATE_LIMITED branch to api.ts alongside the USAGE_LIMIT one (:146 and :250) that surfaces a 'busy, retry in Ns' state and suppresses the automatic retry. Ship the client half on the next `eas update --branch preview` — note phones today run the 97b5f15 bundle, so the backend header is inert on-device until that OTA.
findings.test_first: Backend: `test_rate_limited_response_carries_retry_after` — drive one decorated route past its limit and assert the 429 has a Retry-After header and code=='RATE_LIMITED'. Client: a jest test on the api.ts interceptor asserting a 429 with code 'RATE_LIMITED' produces a distinct typed error (not the generic one) and does not trigger the retry path.
findings.dedupe: new

findings.title: #114 status: leftmost-XFF anchor is a TOTAL bypass (measured 40/40 pass while rotating the header) — correctly HELD, and here is the exact live verification that unblocks it
findings.evidence: _leftmost_xff_ip (rate_limiter.py:33-49) returns `raw.split(",",1)[0].strip()` — the leftmost, i.e. client-supplied, hop; _rate_limit_key (:52-59) uses it whenever ENABLE_PROXY_AWARE_RATELIMIT is on. MEASURED with the real limiter: 40 GETs to a 10/min route sending 'X-Forwarded-For: 8.8.8.<i>, 203.0.113.7' -> 40x200, 0x429; with a FIXED leftmost -> 10x200 then 429.
findings.repro: PYTHONPATH=<repo> python scratchpad/h1.py, output lines E and E2 ('E flagON rotate leftmost XFF 40 -> 200s=40 429s=0', 'E2 flagON fixed leftmost 15 -> 200s=10 429s=5'). Flag set via os.environ['ENABLE_PROXY_AWARE_RATELIMIT']='true' — the module reads it per call, so no reimport is needed.
findings.impact: Confirms the hold is correct and quantifies it: flipping ENABLE_PROXY_AWARE_RATELIMIT as written does not merely weaken the limiter, it removes it — every decorated limit becomes unenforceable by any client willing to send a header, AND admin_audit_log.ip_address (auth_routes.py:437/465/488/506/644, same helper) becomes fully attacker-authored, which is worse than today's useless-but-honest edge IP. Meanwhile the flag is the only thing standing between the deployment and per-client keys, so it also blocks #72 and the whole capacity story.
findings.fix: EXACT LIVE VERIFICATION PROCEDURE for #114, all read-only and all now cheap because the target CIDR is measured (100.64.0.0/10, LS-RATELIMIT-KEY-03). Step 1 — instrument: behind a new default-OFF flag LOG_PROXY_ANCHOR, log one line per request (or 1-in-N) from a place that sees the raw ASGI scope: `anchor peer=%s xff=%r fwd=%r host=%s` with peer=request.client.host, xff=request.headers.get('x-forwarded-for'), fwd=request.headers.get('forwarded'), host=request.headers.get('host'). Put it in RequestIDMiddleware (app/middleware/request_id.py:10-14), which is the OUTERMOST middleware and therefore sees the scope before anything rewrites it. Step 2 — vantage: hit prod from TWO known-distinct public IPs (a phone on cellular and the dev box), each sending NO XFF, then each sending a forged 'X-Forwarded-For: 1.2.3.4'. A handful of requests, not a burst. Step 3 — read the deploy logs for those request_ids (Railway HTTP logs do NOT carry IPs or headers — measured, they are `METHOD PATH STATUS Nms` only — so the app must log it; note deploy logs are retained per-deployment and older deployments are purged, so read them the same day). Step 4 — decide from the data: (a) `peer` must be inside 100.64.0.0/10 for every request, confirming the trust anchor; (b) count the commas in the received `xff` for the no-forgery case — that count IS the hop count, and the real client is at index -(hops trusted); (c) in the forged case, confirm the edge APPENDED the real peer to the RIGHT of '1.2.3.4' — if it did, leftmost is proven attacker-controlled in prod and rightmost-after-trusted is the correct anchor; if the edge REPLACED the header, the leftmost reader is safe and #114 can close as written. Step 5 — implement the winner: prefer `--forwarded-allow-ips=100.64.0.0/10` on the uvicorn start command (railway.json:7) with NO app change, but see LS-RATELIMIT-KEY-11 first — uvicorn's CIDR support is version-dependent and `--proxy-headers` is already on by default, so the flag that actually matters is forwarded-allow-ips. Until steps 1-4 produce data, #114 stays HELD BY DESIGN.
findings.test_first: `test_leftmost_xff_is_not_the_key_when_a_trusted_hop_appended` — construct a request with 'X-Forwarded-For: 1.2.3.4, 203.0.113.9' and assert _rate_limit_key returns 203.0.113.9 (the hop the trusted edge appended), not 1.2.3.4. It fails today. Note tests/test_m13_02_proxy_aware_ratelimit.py:48 `test_flag_on_two_xff_two_keys` currently ASSERTS the broken behaviour, so that test must be inverted as part of the fix.
findings.dedupe: known:#114 (and M13-02 / M18 LS-ratelimit-01 / CLAUDE.md:347) — still-open, HELD BY DESIGN; new here are the measured 40/40 bypass, the measured trust CIDR, and a verification procedure that needs no live egress guessing

findings.title: memory:// storage status: still the only backend, still per-process and restart-wiped, and the redis client needed to fix it is already a pinned dependency
findings.evidence: _get_storage_uri (rate_limiter.py:103-110) has NO Redis branch and no env override: it logs 'Rate limiter using in-memory storage' and returns 'memory://', justified by 'Upstash uses a REST API, not standard Redis protocol' and 'acceptable for a single Railway instance'. Runtime introspection confirms `limiter._storage` is limits.storage.memory.MemoryStorage. requirements.txt:136 pins redis==8.1.0 and :91 limits==5.8.0.
findings.repro: PYTHONPATH=<repo> python scratchpad/h1.py output line F ('F storage=<limits.storage.memory.MemoryStorage object ...> headers_enabled=False ... key_style="url" exempt=set()'), plus reading rate_limiter.py:103-110 at HEAD.
findings.impact: Unchanged since M18 and it is the gating step for everything else in the safe order. Consequences: (a) every Railway deploy, crash or OOM restart resets all buckets to zero, so a redeploy is a free reset of the register/login/account-delete brute-force counters (railway.json sets restartPolicyMaxRetries 3); (b) adding a second uvicorn worker or a second replica — the obvious first response to the single-loop ceiling — silently MULTIPLIES every limit by the worker count, so the capacity fix and the security control fight each other; (c) per-user keys (#72) are pointless without shared storage, because a user's budget would be per-process. The blocking reason given in the comment is real but narrow: the code only knows the REST URL. cache_service.py:23-37 already branches on https:// vs redis://, so the codebase already understands both shapes.
findings.fix: Add a dedicated storage URI env rather than reusing UPSTASH_REDIS_URL (which is the https REST endpoint): read `RATELIMIT_STORAGE_URI` in _get_storage_uri and fall back to 'memory://' when unset, so the default stays byte-identical. Populate it with the Upstash TLS endpoint (rediss://default:<token>@<host>:6379) — Upstash serves both REST and native TLS Redis on the same database, so no new vendor is needed and redis==8.1.0 is already installed. Also set in_memory_fallback=[ANON_LIMIT] and in_memory_fallback_enabled=True in the Limiter constructor at the same time: today swallow_errors=False and the fallback is disabled, so once storage is remote a Redis blip turns every limited request into a 500 rather than degrading. Measure the Upstash RTT from Railway before flipping — the limiter adds one storage round-trip to EVERY request on 61 routes and that RTT has never been measured (M18 gap).
findings.test_first: `test_storage_uri_honours_env_and_defaults_to_memory` — assert _get_storage_uri() returns 'memory://' with the env unset and the exact env value when set. Plus `test_limiter_falls_back_when_storage_raises` — patch the storage to raise and assert the request is served (fallback) rather than 500ing.
findings.dedupe: known:M18 LS-ratelimit-03 (P2) + LS-railway-metrics-04 (P2) + #72 — still-open, unchanged at HEAD; new here is the concrete wiring (RATELIMIT_STORAGE_URI + rediss:// + in_memory_fallback) and that redis is already pinned

findings.title: The prescribed fix is partly a no-op: uvicorn already runs proxy_headers=True, and at uvicorn 0.30 --forwarded-allow-ips does exact-string matching with no CIDR support
findings.evidence: uvicorn source read locally: Config.__init__ has `proxy_headers: bool = True` and `forwarded_allow_ips: ... = None` resolving to `os.environ.get("FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS", "127.0.0.1")`. ProxyHeadersMiddleware.__init__ builds `self.trusted_hosts = {item.strip() for item in trusted_hosts.split(",")}` and get_trusted_client_host tests `if host not in self.trusted_hosts` — exact string membership, no network parsing.
findings.repro: cd <repo> && python -c "import inspect; from uvicorn.config import Config; print(inspect.signature(Config.__init__).parameters['proxy_headers'].default, inspect.signature(Config.__init__).parameters['forwarded_allow_ips'].default)" -> 'True None'; then inspect.getsource(uvicorn.middleware.proxy_headers.ProxyHeadersMiddleware). LOCAL, OFF-LOCK: uvicorn 0.30.0 installed vs uvicorn==0.52.4 pinned at requirements.txt:192.
findings.impact: Every prior write-up of this fix (M13-02's 'Run uvicorn with --proxy-headers --forwarded-allow-ips', M18 LS-ratelimit-01's fix field, CLAUDE.md:347, the M18 W4 lane) prescribes `--proxy-headers` as if it were the missing switch. It is already on. The only switch that matters is --forwarded-allow-ips, and it has two traps that would make a 'fix' silently do nothing while looking shipped: (1) at 0.30-era semantics, passing the measured CIDR `100.64.0.0/10` puts the literal string in a set and matches no peer, so XFF stays discarded and the limiter stays mis-keyed — a green deploy with zero behaviour change; (2) passing `--forwarded-allow-ips='*'` takes the always_trust branch, which returns `x_forwarded_for_hosts[0]` — the LEFTMOST, client-controlled hop — reintroducing exactly the bypass #114 is held for, at the server layer instead of the app layer.
findings.fix: Before touching railway.json:7, determine the pinned version's actual semantics: in the Railway shell or a container built from requirements.txt, run `python -c "import uvicorn,inspect;from uvicorn.middleware.proxy_headers import ProxyHeadersMiddleware;print(uvicorn.__version__);print(inspect.getsource(ProxyHeadersMiddleware))"` and read whether trusted_hosts parses networks. If 0.52.4 supports CIDR, set the start command to `uvicorn app.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port $PORT --forwarded-allow-ips=100.64.0.0/10` (drop --proxy-headers, it is redundant) and NEVER '*'. If it does not, enumerate the observed peers as an explicit comma list, or skip the server layer entirely and do the anchor in _rate_limit_key as rightmost-after-trusted. Either way land it with LS-RATELIMIT-KEY-09's logging so the change is observable rather than assumed.
findings.test_first: `test_uvicorn_trusted_hosts_parses_the_configured_cidr` — a version-pinning test that constructs ProxyHeadersMiddleware(app, trusted_hosts='100.64.0.0/10') and asserts a request whose peer is 100.64.0.7 is trusted. It is the cheapest guard against the silent-no-op deploy and it will fail loudly if a uvicorn bump changes the semantics.
findings.dedupe: new (corrects the fix prescribed by known:M13-02, M18 LS-ratelimit-01 and CLAUDE.md:347 — the mechanism they describe is right, the remedy they name is half no-op and half footgun)

findings.title: Safe order of change, restated with the measured evidence: three of the four prerequisites are now cheap, and step 0 is a metering fix that cannot wait for them
findings.evidence: The premise the current order rests on is written into the code: rate_limiter.py:73-87 'ACTIVATION PRECONDITION: flip this ONLY together with a verified ENABLE_PROXY_AWARE_RATELIMIT so the key is per-client, never the shared proxy IP', echoed at main.py:129-136. Both flags measured ABSENT from Railway `web` (baseline/railway-web-vars.txt), so both are OFF and only the 61 decorators enforce today.
findings.repro: static synthesis over this lane's measurements: experiments A-F (scratchpad/h1.py), the admin_audit_log SELECT (scratchpad/q2.py), the Railway MCP http/deploy log reads, and baseline/railway-web-vars.txt.
findings.impact: The standing ordering rule ('offloads ACTIVE first, because the mis-keyed limiter is the accidental guard on the single loop') is directionally right but rests on a premise this lane measured to be weaker than believed — LS-RATELIMIT-KEY-03 shows >=10 distinct edge-peer buckets, and LS-RATELIMIT-KEY-01/02 show the guard has an unbounded hole at /text/prices/{product} and six other parameterised routes. So the limiter is a leaky guard, not a reliable one, and two items must move OUT of the 'wait for offloads' queue.
findings.fix: SAFE ORDER at HEAD 76ace90. STEP 0 (do NOW, does not wait on anything): meter or gate GET /text/prices/{product} (LS-RATELIMIT-KEY-02) and fix the URL-vs-route bucket key (LS-RATELIMIT-KEY-01) — these CLOSE holes in the current guard, they do not widen it, so the 'offloads first' constraint does not apply; and add the anchor logging from LS-RATELIMIT-KEY-09 plus the audit-table hygiene fix from LS-RATELIMIT-KEY-07, which are read-only instrumentation. STEP 1: offload flags ACTIVE and canaried (#71/#73 — the four W3 flags measured absent, so every hot-path Supabase/Upstash round-trip is still inline on the single loop); nothing that raises effective request throughput may precede this. STEP 2: Redis-backed limiter storage (LS-RATELIMIT-KEY-10 — RATELIMIT_STORAGE_URI + rediss:// + in_memory_fallback), because both a second worker and per-user keys are meaningless while buckets are per-process and restart-wiped; measure Upstash RTT from Railway first, since this adds a round-trip to all 61 routes. STEP 3: verified per-client anchor — run LS-RATELIMIT-KEY-09's procedure, then apply the winner via --forwarded-allow-ips=100.64.0.0/10 (checking LS-RATELIMIT-KEY-11's version trap) or rightmost-after-trusted in _rate_limit_key; this is the step that closes #114 and it is the first step that CHANGES who shares a bucket, so it must not precede STEP 1. STEP 4: per-user keys for authed routes (#72) — only meaningful after STEP 2 (shared storage) and STEP 3 (a real client anchor); key on user_id where present, falling back to the verified IP. STEP 5: ENABLE_DEFAULT_RATE_LIMITS, and only now, because the blanket 10/min on /health and the app-open reads is survivable ONLY with a per-client key (see LS-RATELIMIT-KEY-13). STEP 6: raise the limits, using headers (LS-RATELIMIT-KEY-08) to observe saturation rather than guessing. Do not reorder 3 before 1, and do not treat step 0 as blocked by step 1.
findings.test_first: A CI guard, not a unit test: `test_activation_preconditions_are_documented_and_ordered` reading the flag matrix from CLAUDE.md and asserting ENABLE_DEFAULT_RATE_LIMITS cannot be enabled in a config where ENABLE_PROXY_AWARE_RATELIMIT is off — i.e. make _default_rate_limits_enabled() return False (with a loud log) unless the anchor flag is also on, so the documented precondition is enforced by code instead of by a comment.
findings.dedupe: known:M18 ordering rule (offloads before limiter key) — still-open and RESTATED with measured evidence; the new content is step 0 and the demotion of the limiter from 'the guard' to 'a leaky guard'

findings.title: ENABLE_DEFAULT_RATE_LIMITS activation hazard is sharper than documented: the exempt list is empty, so the blanket 10/min covers /health and can fail a Railway deploy healthcheck
findings.evidence: main.py:137-138 `if _default_rate_limits_enabled(): app.add_middleware(SlowAPIMiddleware)`. Runtime introspection of the real limiter: `_exempt_routes=set()` — nothing is exempt. GET /health is undecorated (main.py:307) so it takes the blanket default. railway.json sets "healthcheckPath": "/health", "healthcheckTimeout": 30, "restartPolicyMaxRetries": 3.
findings.repro: scratchpad/h1.py output line F for the empty exempt set; read main.py:121-138 and :267-310, railway.json at HEAD. Not exercised against prod (flag is OFF there and flipping it is a write).
findings.impact: The code comment (rate_limiter.py:73-87, main.py:129-136) already warns the blanket default would 429 hot reads under a shared key. Two details it does not state and that would bite on activation day: (1) /health is not exempted, and Railway gates the DEPLOY on it — with the shared edge key, any concurrent traffic pushing a path over 10/min while a deploy is healthchecking turns a 429 into a failed healthcheck, a failed deploy and, with restartPolicyMaxRetries 3, a restart loop; the blast radius of a bad flip is the deployment, not just some 429s. (2) Because key_style='url' (LS-RATELIMIT-KEY-01), the blanket default is per CONCRETE path and unmatched 404 paths get their own bucket, so the blanket limit does not bound path scanning at all — the thing a blanket default is usually bought for.
findings.fix: Before ENABLE_DEFAULT_RATE_LIMITS is ever flipped (STEP 5 of the safe order), add the infra paths to the limiter's exempt set — slowapi exposes `@limiter.exempt` on the handler, so decorate main.py:267 favicon, :275 root and :307 health_check — and re-verify `limiter._exempt_routes` is non-empty at startup. Independently, give the Railway healthcheck a path the limiter can never touch. Keep the flag OFF until then; the credential-route protection rides its own decorators and is unaffected.
findings.test_first: `test_health_is_exempt_from_default_limits` — enable ENABLE_DEFAULT_RATE_LIMITS in the fixture, hit GET /health 30 times and assert every response is 200. It fails today (the 11th call would 429), which is precisely the deploy-failure scenario.
findings.dedupe: known:M13-01 / M18 LS-ratelimit-02 (the blanket-default hazard is documented in-code) — still-open; new here are the empty exempt set, the healthcheck-fails-the-deploy consequence, and the per-concrete-path 404 hole

findings.title: P3 sweep: dead limit constants, a false module docstring, no limiter kill switch, and a client-trusted X-Request-ID
findings.evidence: (a) rate_limiter.py:98-100 AUTH_LIMIT/ADMIN_LIMIT/DAILY_LIMIT are referenced by NOTHING except comments and a tautological test (tests/test_security_middleware.py:274-277 asserts 'minute' in AUTH_LIMIT). (b) rate_limiter.py:1 docstring says 'uses slowapi with in-memory storage (Redis optional)' — there is no Redis path (:103-110). (c) Limiter(...) :125-129 passes no `enabled=`, so there is no env kill switch. (d) request_id.py:11 `request.headers.get("X-Request-ID", str(uuid.uuid4()))` echoes any client-supplied correlation id straight back and into every error body.
findings.repro: grep -rn 'AUTH_LIMIT|ADMIN_LIMIT|DAILY_LIMIT' app/ tests/ scripts/ (only rate_limiter.py definitions/comments + the tautological test); read rate_limiter.py:1 and :125-129 and request_id.py:1-15 at HEAD.
findings.impact: (a) Three constants advertise a tiered limit policy (30/min authed, 60/min admin, 100/day) that does not exist — every decorator hardcodes its own string, so a reader tuning AUTH_LIMIT changes nothing; the test that 'covers' them asserts only that a string contains the word 'minute'. (b) A future maintainer looking for the Redis option named in line 1 will not find it. (c) During an incident there is no way to disable the limiter without a redeploy, which matters most in exactly the scenario this lane describes (a shared bucket wrongly 429ing everyone). (d) Two callers sending the same X-Request-ID collide in logs and Sentry, and a caller can deliberately forge another request's id — cheap log poisoning of the only correlation key the error envelope carries.
findings.fix: (a) Delete AUTH_LIMIT/ADMIN_LIMIT/DAILY_LIMIT and the assertion at test_security_middleware.py:274-277, or actually use them at the decorators so one edit retunes a tier. (2) Railway->Supabase and Railway->Upstash RTTs remain UNMEASURED; where I needed an RTT I used M13-06's 163 ms Upstash figure (M18's own anchor) and my dev-box 66 ms warm Supabase figure, and I state the sensitivity. findings.title: Unauthenticated /url/* routes do a blocking socket.getaddrinfo on the event loop per user-supplied URL - measured 11s freeze of the whole deployment per unresolvable host
findings.evidence: url_validator.py:30 `addr_infos = socket.getaddrinfo(hostname, None)` - a synchronous, UNTIMEOUTABLE libc resolver call (getaddrinfo takes no timeout argument and ignores socket.setdefaulttimeout). It is called DIRECTLY from `async def` route bodies with no to_thread: url_routes.py:148 `if not validate_external_url(body.url1) or not validate_external_url(body.url2)` (POST /url/compare), :175 (GET /url/compare), :91/:112 (/url/extract), :197/:216 (/url/detect); and again per redirect hop from url_extraction_service.py:101 and :111 inside `async def fetch_page_html`. MEASURED through the real module (scratchpad/dns.txt): `validate_external_url('https://nonexistent-qaren-probe-9f3a.example/x')` -> 11047 / 11075 / 11258 ms, three consecutive runs (no negative caching); resolvable hosts warm to ~1.4 ms. POST /url/compare calls it TWICE before any work = ~22 s. url_routes.py:128 `async def compare_urls(request, body)` has NO auth dependency and no usage gate.
findings.repro: python -c "import sys;sys.path.insert(0,r'C:/Users/SynAckITPC/Documents/AI/sc-scraper-proof');import time;from app.utils.url_validator import validate_external_url;t=time.perf_counter();validate_external_url('https://nonexistent-qaren-probe-9f3a.example/x');print((time.perf_counter()-t)*1000,'ms')"  -> 11047 ms. Loop-blocking is structural: the call is a plain sync call inside `async def compare_urls` (url_routes.py:148), no await, no to_thread.
findings.impact: Whole-deployment availability. One anonymous HTTP request with two hostnames whose nameservers black-hole freezes the single uvicorn event loop for the full resolver timeout (measured 11 s/host on the dev resolver; glibc default RES_TIMEOUT=5 x RES_DFLRETRY=2 = ~10 s/nameserver on Railway, MODELLED). During the freeze NOTHING else runs - not other users' compares, not /auth/*, not /health. railway.json's healthcheck (30 s) is served by the same loop, so ~3 such requests in flight fail the healthcheck and Railway restarts the only replica (ON_FAILURE, max 3 retries). The route's slowapi limit is 10/min but keyed on the shared Railway edge IP (#114), i.e. 10/min DEPLOYMENT-WIDE - 10 requests x 22 s = 220 s of loop block per 60 s window, a permanent wedge from a single caller. Non-adversarially, any DNS hiccup or a user pasting a dead retailer URL costs every concurrent user 11-22 s of added latency, which the 15 s price race and 30 s STREAM_HARD_CAP convert into TIMEOUTs for unrelated requests.
findings.fix: Move the resolution off the loop and bound it: make `validate_external_url` an `async def` that does `await asyncio.wait_for(asyncio.get_running_loop().getaddrinfo(hostname, None), timeout=2.0)` (the loop's own getaddrinfo already runs in the executor), returning False on TimeoutError/gaierror - and update the 8 call sites in url_routes.py / url_extraction_service.py / price_service.py / shopify_pdp_service.py to await it. Keep a thin sync shim for the warmer/CLI paths. No flag needed: the change is strictly a tighten (a hostname that cannot resolve in 2 s was already going to fail the fetch), but if a flag is wanted, gate the 2 s ceiling behind ENABLE_SSRF_RESOLVE_TIMEOUT and leave the offload unconditional. Ship BEFORE any /url/* traffic and before the #114 limiter re-key, since re-keying raises the per-caller ceiling on this path.
findings.test_first: tests/test_url_validator_offloop.py: monkeypatch socket.getaddrinfo to `lambda *a, **k: time.sleep(3) or []`, then in an asyncio test start a background `asyncio.sleep(0)` heartbeat task that stamps time.monotonic() every 10 ms, call the /url/compare handler via httpx.ASGITransport with a bogus host, and assert the heartbeat gap never exceeds 200 ms. RED today (gap == 3 s x2).
findings.dedupe: new (adjacent to mobile-checkup lead 'POST /url/compare unmetered+no history' and to #114's limiter key, but neither names the on-loop resolver; url_validator.py is in no prior review's file list)

findings.title: supabase create_client() runs per request and sits OUTSIDE the run_db lambda, so both offload flags leave a 355ms certifi SSL-context build plus a cold connection pool on the event loop
findings.evidence: auth_service.py:30 `return create_client(SUPABASE_URL, SUPABASE_ANON_KEY)` and :37 (admin) build a NEW client on every call - unlike database_service.py:38-45 which memoizes `_admin_client`. database_service.py:52 `get_user_supabase_client` also builds one per call. Critically the construction is OUTSIDE the offload lambda: auth_service.py:256-257 is `client = get_auth_client()` then `await run_db(lambda: client.auth.get_user(access_token))`, so run_db offloads the RTT and leaves the construction inline. MEASURED by profile (scratchpad/prof.txt): 344 of 354 ms per create_client is `_ssl._SSLContext.load_verify_locations` under httpx `_config.load_ssl_context_verify` - the certifi CA bundle parsed fresh for each of the client's httpx sessions. Steady-state timing over 10 calls: 686/343/405/377/370/401/385/369/285/310 ms. Measured effect on the wire (scratchpad/rtt.txt, dev box -> prod Supabase): reused client query = 63-69 ms; fresh create_client = 348-436 ms of CPU, and that fresh client's first query = 456-604 ms (no keep-alive to reuse). Probe counts per request (scratchpad/probe_on.txt, BOTH offload flags ON): /auth/verify 1 ON-LOOP create_client, /auth/me 2, /usage/status 2, /comparisons/history 2, /home/savings 1, /home/smart-pick 1, /auth/refresh 2, /auth/login 3.
findings.repro: python scratchpad/probe.py out.txt on  (runs the real app.main through TestClient; every create_client line is tagged @ON-LOOP even with ENABLE_SYNC_DB_OFFLOAD=true). Cost: python -c "import time;from supabase import create_client;[print((lambda t:(create_client('https://x.supabase.co','k'),(time.perf_counter()-t)*1000)[1])(time.perf_counter())) for _ in range(5)]"
findings.impact: This is the single largest per-request loop cost that neither offload flag can remove, and it is the one nobody has costed. Even at a conservative Linux/Railway estimate of 20-60 ms per SSL-context load (MODELLED; the 355 ms figure is dev-box Windows), an app-open burst of 4 authed reads costs 7 create_clients = 140-420 ms of pure CPU on the only loop, on top of every RTT M18 already counted; at the dev-box figure it is 2.5 s. Because no client is ever reused or closed, every Supabase call also pays a fresh TCP+TLS handshake instead of keep-alive (measured +390 to +540 ms end-to-end on this box) and leaks an unclosed httpx pool per request until GC. Flipping ENABLE_SYNC_DB_OFFLOAD - the whole point of #115/#116 - therefore buys much less than the flag's docstring claims (db_offload.py:1-8 says it moves 'the REQUEST-PATH HOT SET' off the loop).
findings.fix: Memoize both auth_service factories the way database_service.py:38-45 already memoizes admin: module-level `_auth_client`/`_admin_client` singletons behind a lock, and replace `get_user_supabase_client(token)` with the cached anon client plus a per-call `postgrest.auth(token)` on a request-scoped shallow wrapper (or drop to `get_admin_supabase_client()` + explicit .eq(user_id) filters where RLS is not actually load-bearing). Pass `ClientOptions(postgrest_client_timeout=...)` at the same time (see finding 04). If the risk of sharing a mutated postgrest auth header across concurrent requests is a concern, keep a small keyed pool of anon clients rather than one-per-request. Ship unflagged - the construction is pure setup with no behavioural fork - but land it BEFORE flipping ENABLE_SYNC_DB_OFFLOAD so the flag's measured benefit is not swamped by this.
findings.test_first: tests/test_supabase_client_reuse.py: patch supabase.create_client with a counter, drive GET /auth/me and GET /usage/status through TestClient twice each, assert the counter increments at most once per distinct (url, key) pair for the whole test (currently 2 per request, 8 total).
findings.dedupe: new (M18 LS-capacity-math-02's verify_reason notes in passing that the user-scoped client is 'a new create_client per call vs cached admin', but it is not a finding, the auth_service factories are not named, the outside-the-lambda placement is not observed, and the SSL-context cost was never quantified)

findings.title: The Upstash client is built with library defaults: httpx.Client(timeout=None) plus a 3-second time.sleep retry - a stalled Upstash blocks the single event loop forever, and any transient error freezes it 3s per command
findings.evidence: cache_service.py:28 `redis_client = Redis(url=UPSTASH_REDIS_URL, token=UPSTASH_REDIS_TOKEN)` - no rest_retries, no rest_retry_interval, no timeout. Verified inside the LOCKED wheel (requirements.txt:186 `upstash-redis==1.7.0`, downloaded from PyPI to scratchpad/up17): upstash_redis/client.py:39-40 defaults `rest_retries: int = 1`, `rest_retry_interval: float = 3`; upstash_redis/http.py:54 `self._client = httpx.Client(timeout=None)`; http.py:68-82 `for attempts_left in range(...): try: r = self._client.post(...) except Exception: ... if attempts_left > 0: time.sleep(self._retry_interval)`. Confirmed at runtime on the installed 1.6.0: `r._http._client.timeout` -> `Timeout(timeout=None)`, `retries 1 interval 3`. Under PROD flags (ENABLE_ASYNC_REDIS_OFFLOAD absent from railway-web-vars.txt) every one of these runs inline: probe_off.txt shows redis.get/setex tagged @ON-LOOP on /auth/verify, /auth/me, /usage/status x3, /home/trending, /home/savings, /home/smart-pick and /auth/login.
findings.repro: static + library-source. `python -c "from upstash_redis import Redis; r=Redis(url='https://x',token='t'); print(r._http._client.timeout, r._http._retries, r._http._retry_interval)"` -> `Timeout(timeout=None) 1 3`; and unzip the pinned 1.7.0 wheel: `python -c "import zipfile;print(zipfile.ZipFile('up17/upstash_redis-1.7.0-py3-none-any.whl').read('upstash_redis/http.py').decode().splitlines()[53])"` -> `        self._client = httpx.Client(timeout=None)`. Not exercised against live Upstash (brief forbids prod Redis writes and a fault injection).
findings.impact: Two distinct whole-deployment failure modes that no timeout anywhere in the app can bound. (a) NO TIMEOUT: if an Upstash POST stalls (TLS hang, black-holed route, provider incident), the sync httpx call never returns and the single uvicorn loop is blocked until the OS TCP stack gives up - minutes, not seconds. /health is served by that same loop, so the Railway 30 s healthcheck fails and the only replica restarts; on restart the first authed request hits the same stall. (b) RETRY SLEEP: on any raised exception the library does `time.sleep(3)` ON THE EVENT LOOP. M18 counts 40-60 Upstash commands per cold compare; a flapping Upstash therefore converts one compare into up to 3 minutes of frozen loop. This also silently breaks every wall-clock budget in the system (the 15 s price race, STREAM_HARD_CAP_SECONDS=30) because those measure elapsed time while the loop is not running.
findings.fix: Construct the client explicitly: `Redis(url=..., token=..., rest_retries=0, rest_retry_interval=0)` and then force a bounded transport - `redis_client._http._client = httpx.Client(timeout=httpx.Timeout(2.0, connect=1.0))` immediately after construction (the library exposes no timeout kwarg in 1.7.0), or wrap the module's `_redis_get`/`_redis_set`/`_redis_incr`/`_redis_expire` helpers so each command runs under a bounded budget. Every cache helper is already fail-open on exception (cache_service.py:62-64, 77-79), so a timeout degrades to a cache miss, which is the intended behaviour. This is a hard prerequisite for flipping ENABLE_ASYNC_REDIS_OFFLOAD too: off-loop a hung command still parks a pool thread forever and drains the 40-thread executor.
findings.test_first: tests/test_cache_service_timeout.py: assert `cache_service.redis_client._http._client.timeout.read is not None and <= 2.0` and `redis_client._http._retries == 0`; plus a loop-starvation test that patches the transport to sleep 3 s, calls `_redis_get` from an async test with a 10 ms heartbeat task, and asserts the heartbeat gap stays under 200 ms.
findings.dedupe: new (M18/M13 costed Upstash RTT at 163 ms and flagged the calls as on-loop, but no prior finding notes that the client has no timeout at all or that the retry path sleeps 3 s on the loop; no open issue covers it - #71 is about moving Redis off the loop, not bounding it)

findings.title: Every Supabase client is left at postgrest's 120-second default timeout, so one slow query freezes the whole loop for 4x the Railway healthcheck window
findings.evidence: All four construction sites pass only (url, key) and no ClientOptions: database_service.py:44, :52 and auth_service.py:30, :37 (grep for ClientOptions/postgrest_client_timeout across app/ returns zero hits). In the LOCKED wheels: postgrest-2.31.0 `postgrest/constants.py:6 DEFAULT_POSTGREST_CLIENT_TIMEOUT = 120`, and supabase-2.31.0 `supabase/lib/client_options.py:54 postgrest_client_timeout: ... = DEFAULT_POSTGREST_CLIENT_TIMEOUT`, threaded to the transport at `supabase/_sync/client.py:188 timeout=self.options.postgrest_client_timeout`. Confirmed at runtime on the installed 2.28.0: `create_client(...).postgrest.session.timeout` -> `Timeout(timeout=120)` (the GoTrue side is bounded at 5 s: `.auth._http_client.timeout` -> `Timeout(timeout=5.0)`). Under PROD flags all 129 async-def `.execute()` calls run inline on the loop (db_offload.py:38-40 returns `call()` with no await when the flag is off).
findings.repro: python -c "from supabase import create_client; c=create_client('https://x.supabase.co','k'); print(c.postgrest.session.timeout)" -> Timeout(timeout=120); and `python -c "import zipfile;print([l for l in zipfile.ZipFile('sb31/postgrest-2.31.0-py3-none-any.whl').read('postgrest/constants.py').decode().splitlines() if 'TIMEOUT' in l])"` -> DEFAULT_POSTGREST_CLIENT_TIMEOUT = 120.
findings.impact: A single degraded Supabase query - a missing index on the unbounded /home/savings scan, a Supabase incident, a connection reset that hangs mid-read - blocks the single event loop for up to 120 s. railway.json's healthcheck timeout is 30 s and Procfile runs one uvicorn worker with no --workers, so the deployment is DOWN and then restarted for the whole window, taking every in-flight compare with it. Flipping ENABLE_SYNC_DB_OFFLOAD does not fix this: it converts a 120 s loop freeze into a 120 s occupied thread out of 40 (executor.py:30), so ~40 such queries exhaust the shared pool that the ~18-way adapter fan-out also draws on. Note the asymmetry that makes this easy to miss: the GoTrue leg IS bounded at 5 s, so verify_token behaves while the data-plane does not.
findings.fix: Pass explicit options at all four construction sites: `create_client(url, key, options=ClientOptions(postgrest_client_timeout=httpx.Timeout(8.0, connect=3.0), storage_client_timeout=8))` - 8 s comfortably exceeds the measured warm query (66 ms) and every history/savings scan, while staying under the 15 s price race and the 30 s stream cap so a stalled DB degrades to the existing except-branches (every one of these call sites already catches Exception and returns a default). Land it in the same change as finding 02's client memoization, since both edit the same four lines. Unflagged - a bounded timeout cannot change behaviour for any query that currently succeeds.
findings.test_first: tests/test_supabase_client_timeouts.py::test_postgrest_timeout_is_bounded - `assert database_service.get_admin_supabase_client().postgrest.session.timeout.read <= 10` and the same for auth_service.get_auth_client()/get_admin_client(). RED today (120).
findings.dedupe: new (M18 LS-event-loop-09 notes only that the healthcheck shares the blocked loop; no prior finding identifies the 120 s postgrest default or the absence of ClientOptions)

findings.title: The M18 fix that parallelised the freemium gate's two Supabase reads with asyncio.gather is INERT in the shipped flag state - run_db never yields when ENABLE_SYNC_DB_OFFLOAD is off, so they still run serially
findings.evidence: usage_service.py:348-352: `# LS-event-loop-03: the two Supabase reads are independent of each other - fetch them concurrently instead of serially.` / `user_info, bonus = await asyncio.gather(_get_user_tier_info(user_id), _get_active_referral_bonus(user_id))`. Both coroutines reach Supabase only through `await run_db(lambda: ...execute())` (usage_service.py:530 and :607, both confirmed by the probe). db_offload.py:35-40: `async def run_db(call): if sync_db_offload_enabled(): return await asyncio.to_thread(call); return call()` - the flag-off branch has NO await, and the module's own docstring says so at line 12-14 ('runs the call synchronously to completion with no new suspension point'). A coroutine with no suspension point runs to completion inside gather's first step, so gather executes them one after the other. Railway has neither offload var set (baseline/railway-web-vars.txt), so this is the shipped state. Probe confirms both executes @ON-LOOP under flags-off and @off-loop under flags-on (probe_off.txt vs probe_on.txt, /usage/status).
findings.repro: static, from the runtime module: `python -c "import asyncio,time; from app.utils.db_offload import run_db; async def m(): t=time.perf_counter(); await asyncio.gather(run_db(lambda: time.sleep(0.2)), run_db(lambda: time.sleep(0.2))); print((time.perf_counter()-t)*1000)" ` with ENABLE_SYNC_DB_OFFLOAD unset -> ~400 ms (serial); with it =true -> ~200 ms.
findings.impact: Every authed compare (POST/GET /text/compare, GET /text/compare/stream) opens with this gate. The M18 remediation is recorded as closing LS-event-loop-03, and the code reads as if the two round trips overlap, but in production they do not - the gate still costs two full serialized Supabase RTTs plus two create_clients before any comparison work starts, exactly as before. The wider lesson for this campaign: any 'concurrency' fix expressed as gather/as_completed over run_db-wrapped work is a no-op until ENABLE_SYNC_DB_OFFLOAD is on, so the flag is not merely a latency knob - it is load-bearing for correctness of the parallelism claims. Nothing regressed; the win was simply never delivered.
findings.fix: Either (a) make the parallelism unconditional by having the two readers use `asyncio.to_thread` directly rather than run_db - the calls are pure reads with no ordering constraint, so there is no flag-off behaviour to preserve; or (b) leave the code as-is and correct the record: annotate usage_service.py:348 with 'this gather only parallelises when ENABLE_SYNC_DB_OFFLOAD is ON' and move LS-event-loop-03 from closed to gated-on-#115. Option (a) is preferable and cheap. Whichever is chosen, audit the other gather/as_completed sites over run_db-wrapped coroutines for the same inertness before crediting them.
findings.test_first: tests/test_usage_gate_parallel.py: with ENABLE_SYNC_DB_OFFLOAD unset, patch `usage_service._get_user_tier_info` and `_get_active_referral_bonus` to record entry/exit timestamps via a blocking 100 ms sleep inside their run_db lambda, call consume_comparison_credit, and assert the two intervals OVERLAP. RED today (they are disjoint).
findings.dedupe: known:M18/LS-event-loop-03 - reported as fixed, actually still-open in the shipped flag state; the inertness of gather-over-run_db is new

findings.title: Hybrid model routing adds 3 blocking Upstash commands to every compare's verdict phase, in neither offload set and inside the stream deadline
findings.evidence: ENABLE_HYBRID_MODEL_ROUTING=true in prod (baseline/railway-web-vars.txt). extraction_service.py:2331 `verdict_model = await model_router.get_model(priority="high")` -> model_router_service.py:61 `used = await self._get_4o_usage_today()` -> :89 `raw = _redis_get(self._get_counter_key())` (a direct cache_service helper, NOT a `*_async` dispatch). extraction_service.py:2501 `await model_router.record_usage(verdict_model, tokens_used)` -> :107 `redis_client.incrby(key, int(tokens_used))` and :108 `_redis_expire(key, self._COUNTER_TTL)`. The AST census lists model_router_service.py:107 among the 10 raw `redis_client.*` calls inside an `async def` with no enclosing offload lambda (scratchpad/ast2.txt). Neither ENABLE_ASYNC_REDIS_OFFLOAD nor ENABLE_SYNC_DB_OFFLOAD reaches this module - it imports `_redis_get`/`_redis_expire` from cache_service directly (model_router_service.py:21) and pulls `redis_client` inline at :102.
findings.repro: static (no live compare is possible - OpenAI returns 429 insufficient_quota at review time). Chain verified by reading extraction_service.py:2331/2501 and model_router_service.py:61/89/95-108 at HEAD; the module is absent from the `_redis_offload_enabled` grep (which returns cache_service, auth_service, usage_service, home_routes, review_service, serper_service, structured_comparison_service, feedback_service only).
findings.impact: 3 blocking Upstash round trips per compare that M18's 40-60 command count did not include and that neither offload flag can remove. At M13-06's measured 163 ms Upstash RTT that is ~490 ms of frozen loop per comparison; at a 5 ms same-region RTT it is 15 ms (SENSITIVITY: the Railway->Upstash RTT is unmeasured, so this ranges 15-490 ms). It lands in the worst place - the verdict phase, inside STREAM_HARD_CAP_SECONDS=30 - so under any concurrency it eats the budget of the very request that is nearly done, and it steals from every other in-flight compare's wall-clock race. Secondary: because the counter read fails open to 0 (:92-93), a stalled Upstash both freezes the loop AND silently disables the daily gpt-4o token cap, so the cost guard is off exactly when the system is unhealthy.
findings.fix: Give model_router the same module-local offload dispatch pattern the rest of the codebase uses (the `_is_token_revoked_async` / `_atomic_consume_async` idiom): add `async def _read_4o_usage_async()` / `_increment_4o_usage_async()` that call the existing sync helpers via `asyncio.to_thread` when `_redis_offload_enabled()` and inline otherwise, referencing the module-level symbols in both branches so tests that patch them intercept either path. Better still, cache the daily counter in a process-local variable with a short TTL (the cap is 1,000,000 tokens/day - a 30 s staleness is irrelevant) so the read costs nothing on the common path and only the INCRBY touches Upstash. Inert flag-off; no new flag required.
findings.test_first: tests/test_model_router_offload.py: with ENABLE_ASYNC_REDIS_OFFLOAD=true, patch model_router_service._redis_get to record whether `asyncio.get_running_loop()` succeeds, `await model_router.get_model(priority='high')`, and assert it did NOT run on the loop. RED today.
findings.dedupe: new (M18 LS-event-loop-05 covers review_service and the provider budget gates; model_router_service is named in no prior finding and in no open issue)

findings.title: GET /comparisons/history pulls every row's full full_response (measured 19KB p50 x up to 50 rows) to compute a winner index, then runs a second unwrapped full-table count on the loop
findings.evidence: database_service.py:248-260 `client.table("comparisons").select("*")...` then `await run_db(lambda: query.range(offset, offset+limit-1).execute())` - `select("*")` includes the `full_response` JSONB. history_routes.py:106-125 uses those rows for exactly four scalars: `_extract_winner_index(full)` and `_extract_winner_runner_up_image_urls(full, winner_index)`, plus id/query/product_names/input_type/created_at. Then history_routes.py:127 `total = await get_user_comparison_count(...)` -> database_service.py:449-455 `client.table("comparisons").select("id", count="exact").eq("user_id",...).eq("schema_version",2).execute()` - a bare execute, outside run_db, i.e. inline under BOTH flags (probe_on.txt: `supabase.execute database_service.py:454 @ON-LOOP`). MEASURED payload from the live comparisons table (read-only SELECT, scratchpad/sizes.txt): 27 rows, full_response bytes min=80, p50=19026, max=24992, sum=484778.
findings.repro: python scratchpad/probe.py out.txt on ; grep -A8 'comparisons/history' out.txt -> 4 ON-LOOP sites with both flags ON, two of them create_client and one the count execute. Payload: supabase select('id, full_response, created_at').limit(30) against prod -> p50 19 KB/row.
findings.impact: The default page is limit=20 and the cap is limit=50 (history_routes.py:92), so a single history open transfers roughly 20 x 19 KB = 380 KB (worst case 50 x 25 KB = 1.25 MB) from Supabase and JSON-deserializes it on the event loop, to produce three integers and two image URLs per row. The deserialization is CPU on the only loop and is invisible to both offload flags (the parse happens after run_db returns). The count query is a second round trip that scans every id the user owns and is itself inline on the loop under both flags, so scrolling history is 2 create_clients + 1 large transfer + 1 unwrapped scan per page. Same defect family as LS-event-loop-01 (/home/savings) and LS-event-loop-06 (/home/smart-pick) but on a different route that neither finding names, and history_routes.py/database_service.py were both edited in the M21 window without it being caught.
findings.fix: Narrow the projection to what the route reads. Either (a) add generated/persisted columns for winner_index + the two image URLs at save time (save_comparison already validates renderability at database_service.py:64) and `select("id, query, product_names, input_type, created_at, winner_index, winner_image_url, runner_up_image_url")`; or (b) short term, keep full_response but ask PostgREST for just the sub-paths the extractors need (`select("id,query,product_names,input_type,created_at,full_response->products,full_response->comparison")`). Separately, wrap database_service.py:449-455 in run_db, and replace the exact count with `count="planned"` or drop it in favour of a has-more boolean derived from `len(rows) == limit` - an exact total is not rendered as a number the user acts on.
findings.test_first: tests/test_history_projection.py: patch get_user_supabase_client with a fake whose `.select(cols)` records the column string, call GET /comparisons/history, and assert `'*' not in cols and 'full_response' not in cols`; plus assert `database_service.get_user_comparison_count` runs off-loop when ENABLE_SYNC_DB_OFFLOAD=true. Both RED today.
findings.dedupe: new (the payload-shape defect is the same class as M18 LS-event-loop-01/-06 but on /comparisons/history, which neither names; MB-contract-04 covers history winner_index correctness, not the projection or the count scan)

findings.title: STATUS: /home/savings still runs the unbounded all-rows full_response scan in prod - the #116 aggregate path is dark and its migration is unapplied
findings.evidence: home_routes.py:219 `if _home_savings_aggregate_enabled():` gates the one-round-trip RPC path; :63-65 reads `ENABLE_HOME_SAVINGS_AGGREGATE`, which does NOT appear in baseline/railway-web-vars.txt (54 vars listed for `web`) -> OFF in prod. home_routes.py:245-247 states the flag-off fallback plainly: `# Flag-OFF fallback - the pre-#116 Python-side scan, kept byte-identical ... Unbounded in rows and payload - that is exactly why the aggregate path above exists; do not extend this branch.` The RPC it would call (`home_savings_aggregate`) lives in migrations/036_home_savings_aggregate.sql, which the brief records as written but NOT applied (alongside 033/034/035). The scan's SELECT is at least now run_db-wrapped (probe_on.txt shows `home_routes.py:255 <- db_offload.py:40 @off-loop` with the flag on), but under prod flags it is @ON-LOOP (probe_off.txt), and the create_client at :215 is @ON-LOOP in both states.

findings.impact: M18 rated this P1 and it is unchanged in the shipped state: /home/savings is called on every Home render for an authed user and reads every schema_version=2 row that user owns, full_response included, then sums in Python. At the measured 19 KB/row p50 a heavy user's Home open is a multi-hundred-KB transfer plus a full JSON parse on the only event loop, growing without bound as the user's history grows. Two independent preconditions block the fix, and neither is a code change: migration 036 must be applied to Supabase, then ENABLE_HOME_SAVINGS_AGGREGATE must be set on the `web` service. Reporting it so the activation checklist does not assume #116 shipped a benefit.

Order matters: flipping the flag before the migration lands makes every call take the except-branch at home_routes.py:227-231 and silently return the empty payload (savings 0, threshold_met false), i.e. a silent product regression rather than an error.

findings.title: STATUS: the token-revocation Redis GET on every authed request is now offloadable but still inline in the shipped flag state, and the create_client immediately after it never was
findings.evidence: The #115 remediation landed: auth_service.py:321-332 `_is_token_revoked_async` dispatches to `asyncio.to_thread(_is_token_revoked, token)` when `_redis_offload_enabled()`, and verify_token calls it at :252. Probe confirms the fix works when the flag is on (probe_on.txt: `redis.get auth_service.py:315:_is_token_revoked @off-loop(thread=asyncio_0)`) and is inert when off (probe_off.txt: same site `@ON-LOOP`). ENABLE_ASYNC_REDIS_OFFLOAD does not appear in baseline/railway-web-vars.txt, so prod is the inline branch - M18's LS-event-loop-04 is unchanged in production. Separately, the very next two lines are NOT covered by either flag: :256 `client = get_auth_client()` (a full create_client, ON-LOOP in both probe runs) then :257 `await run_db(lambda: client.auth.get_user(access_token))`.
findings.repro: diff the two probe runs on the /auth/verify block: flags-off `total blocking-io sites=3 (ON-LOOP=3)`, flags-on `(ON-LOOP=1, offloaded=2)` - the residual 1 is the create_client at auth_service.py:30.
findings.impact: Every authenticated request to every route pays this prologue - the probe shows it on /auth/verify, /auth/me, /usage/status, /comparisons/history, /home/savings, /home/smart-pick and (via get_optional_user) on all four compare entry points. In the shipped flag state that is 1 blocking Upstash GET + 1 SSL-context build + 1 GoTrue RTT serialized on the only loop before the handler body starts. Flipping ENABLE_ASYNC_REDIS_OFFLOAD removes the Upstash leg and ENABLE_SYNC_DB_OFFLOAD removes the GoTrue leg, but the client construction survives both (finding 02) - so the best achievable app-open prologue without a code change is still one on-loop create_client per request.
findings.fix: Two steps. (1) Flip ENABLE_ASYNC_REDIS_OFFLOAD and ENABLE_SYNC_DB_OFFLOAD on the `web` service - but only after findings 03 (bound the Upstash client) and 04 (bound the postgrest client) land, because off-loop an untimeouted call parks a pool thread forever instead of the loop, and the 40-thread executor (executor.py:30) is shared with the ~18-way adapter fan-out. (2) Memoize get_auth_client per finding 02 so the residual goes to zero. Keep the ordering rule M18 pinned: offloads active and verified before the #114 limiter re-key.

findings.title: P3 sweep: middleware cost, uncached curated-trending read, shared-Upstash-client thread state, and four routes verified clean
findings.evidence: (a) MEASURED middleware chain cost (scratchpad/mw.txt): a bare FastAPI app vs the same app with RequestIDMiddleware + SecurityHeadersMiddleware + ErrorHandlerMiddleware + CORSMiddleware, 300 requests each after 30 warmups -> bare mean 1.909 ms / p95 2.445 ms, with-middleware mean 2.626 ms / p95 3.368 ms, delta 0.717 ms/request. All three are starlette BaseHTTPMiddleware, each of which wraps the call in an anyio task group + memory object stream; none does I/O; error_handler.py:152-155 imports sentry_sdk only on the exception path. slowapi is memory:// (rate_limiter.py:103-110) and its key_func (:52-59) reads only request headers - no storage I/O, no blocking; SlowAPIMiddleware is not even registered in prod (main.py:137, ENABLE_DEFAULT_RATE_LIMITS unset). Verdict: real but ~1000x smaller than any I/O site here; not worth changing. (b) home_routes.py:712-733 `_load_curated_trending()` has no lru_cache and does `open(_TRENDING_CURATED_PATH) / json.load(fh)` plus a full re-validation loop on every /home/trending cache miss, on the loop - contrast price_service.py:8413 `@functools.lru_cache(maxsize=1)` on the analogous variant-hint reference load, and review_service.py:466-470 / cohort_service.py:67-68 which both memoize. (c) upstash_redis is constructed with `read_your_writes=True` (library default), so the single module-global client at cache_service.py:28 carries a mutable `self._sync_token` that every command reads and rewrites; with ENABLE_ASYNC_REDIS_OFFLOAD ON up to 40 pool threads mutate it concurrently - benign for correctness (worst case a read is sent with a stale sync token) but it is undeclared shared state across the offload boundary. (d) VERIFIED CLEAN, no change needed: GET /health (main.py:307-313, 0 I/O sites in both probe runs - correct for a 30 s Railway healthcheck), GET / (main.py:275), GET /api/v1/app/version (version_routes.py:8-16, env reads only), GET /api/v1/legal/* (0 sites); the per-request `get_comparison_service()` (structured_comparison_service.py:8044-8046 -> __init__ at :2602-2652 is 12 plain assignments, no I/O); all 22 curl_cffi fetches sit inside `asyncio.to_thread` lambdas; OpenAI uses AsyncOpenAI with cached clients and an explicit httpx.Timeout(120, connect=30) (openai_service.py:32-34, 46-77).
findings.repro: Middleware: the benchmark script recorded in scratchpad/mw.txt (two TestClient apps, 300 requests each). (b)/(c): static read at HEAD. (d): python scratchpad/probe.py out.txt off|on - /health, /app/version and /legal/privacy report `total blocking-io sites=0` in both runs.
findings.impact: (a) ~0.72 ms of pure loop time per request is a ~1400 req/s ceiling from the middleware alone - three orders of magnitude above the I/O-bound ceilings in findings 01-04, so it is not a lever; recording it so nobody spends the effort. (b) a few hundred microseconds of file I/O + parse per trending cache miss (TTL 1 h per region, 6 regions) - trivial, but it is the only un-memoized data-file read left on a request path and it will grow with the curated list. (c) latent only, and only after ENABLE_ASYNC_REDIS_OFFLOAD flips. (d) the clean results matter as much as the defects: /health doing zero I/O is what keeps the Railway healthcheck honest, and it must stay that way - findings 01/03/04 are all about work that can starve that same loop, not about /health itself.
findings.fix: (b) add `@functools.lru_cache(maxsize=1)` to `_load_curated_trending` (home_routes.py:712) matching the price_service.py:8413 precedent, and document that changing data/trending_curated.json needs a redeploy - which is already true, it ships in the image. (c) when ENABLE_ASYNC_REDIS_OFFLOAD is flipped, either pass `read_your_writes=False` at cache_service.py:28 (nothing in this codebase depends on read-your-writes across commands) or give each pool thread its own client. (a) no action. (d) add a regression test that pins /health to zero I/O so a future 'let's check the DB in the healthcheck' change is caught - that is the only durable protection for the 30 s healthcheck budget.

findings.title: The Upstash client has NO timeout and a 3s blocking sleep-retry, so a slow/hung Upstash never raises: every fail-open except block is unreachable and the single event loop stalls forever
findings.evidence: cache_service.py:28 `redis_client = Redis(url=UPSTASH_REDIS_URL, token=UPSTASH_REDIS_TOKEN)` -- no timeout arg, and the SDK exposes none. Railway deploy log (MCP get_logs, service web) confirms the branch taken: '[2026-09-02T15:54:16Z] Upstash Redis (REST) client initialized'. Inspected the LOCKED wheel (pip download upstash-redis==1.7.0, requirements.txt:186): upstash_redis/http.py:54 `self._client = httpx.Client(timeout=None)`; http.py:82 `time.sleep(self._retry_interval)`; client.py:39-40 `rest_retries: int = 1, rest_retry_interval: float = 3`. The redis:// fallback branch (cache_service.py:36) is no better: redis.from_url with no socket_timeout also defaults to None.
findings.repro: python -c to unzip pkg/upstash_redis-1.7.0-py3-none-any.whl and grep httpx.Client / time.sleep in upstash_redis/http.py (done, scratchpad/lane/pkg). Railway MCP get_logs service=web search=Redis returns the REST-client init line. Static for the hang itself: HARD RULE forbids load/fault injection against prod Upstash.
findings.impact: Every Redis-dependent handler (cache read, freemium gate, budget gate, token revocation) calls a BLOCKING httpx POST with no deadline on the single uvicorn worker's event loop (ENABLE_ASYNC_REDIS_OFFLOAD is absent from all 54 Railway `web` vars, so the #115 offload dispatches are inert). During an Upstash slowdown/partition the process does not fail open -- it fails HANG: the whole deployment (1 replica x 1 worker) stops answering /health, /auth/me, /usage/status and every compare, and Railway's ON_FAILURE restart budget (max 3) is the only recovery. On a connection ERROR the SDK sleeps 3s synchronously then retries once, so a cold compare's ~30-70 commands become up to 90-210s of event-loop freeze inside a 30s STREAM_HARD_CAP. This is the root reason the M18 'everything fails open' thesis is wrong in the worst case.
findings.fix: At client construction in cache_service.py, replace the SDK's default transport with a bounded one and disable the sleep-retry: `redis_client = Redis(url=..., token=..., rest_retries=0)` then `redis_client._http._client = httpx.Client(timeout=httpx.Timeout(connect=1.0, read=2.0, write=2.0, pool=1.0))`. Gate the whole thing behind a new default-ON-after-canary flag ENABLE_UPSTASH_TIMEOUT (read per call at init only, so a bad value can be reverted by redeploy) and log the effective timeout once at startup like the serper gate does. With a real timeout the existing `except Exception -> fail-open` blocks finally do what their docstrings claim. Do this BEFORE flipping ENABLE_ASYNC_REDIS_OFFLOAD, or a hang just moves into the 40-thread executor and exhausts it instead.
findings.test_first: tests/test_upstash_client_timeout.py: build the client through cache_service's own init path with a stub URL, assert `redis_client._http._client.timeout.read is not None` and `redis_client._http._retries == 0`. Second red test: monkeypatch cache_service.redis_client with a fake whose .get() sleeps 5s, run `asyncio.wait_for(auth_service._is_token_revoked_async(tok), timeout=3)` and assert it raises TimeoutError today (proving no internal deadline) and returns False (fail-open) after the fix.
