findings.title: P3 sweep: five smaller concurrency defects found while walking the surface
findings.evidence: (a) UNBOUNDED BACKGROUND FAN-OUT — async_utils.py:54 `task = asyncio.create_task(coro)` with 41 `fire_and_forget(...)` call sites across app/. There is no cap, no counter and no drain: each request spawns several background tasks (log_search, log_audit_event, save_comparison_and_track_cohort, push delivery, behavior-profile writeback) that then do synchronous Supabase/Upstash work on the same loop, so background work from request N competes with foreground work from request N+1 with no ordering or backpressure. (b) NO SHUTDOWN PATH — the app has exactly ONE lifecycle handler (main.py:168, the executor install) and no shutdown counterpart: the ThreadPoolExecutor is never explicitly drained and the memoised AsyncOpenAI/Supabase clients are never closed, so a Railway SIGTERM abandons in-flight adapter threads mid-`curl.perform()`. (c) SECOND UNCOUNTED THREAD POOL — 22 routes depend on the sync `verify_admin_key` (admin_routes.py:34), 3 on the sync `_extract_token` (history_routes.py:26) and 1 on `_require_referral_enabled` (referral_routes.py:57); FastAPI runs sync dependencies on anyio's threadpool, a SECOND 40-token pool that executor.py's sizing rationale does not mention. Trivial cost today (header compares) but it is an unmodelled resource. (d) UNBOUNDED THROTTLE DICT — shopify_pdp_service.py:113 `_next_slot_at: Dict[str, float] = {}` is never pruned; finding 07's fix should prune it. (e) DEPRECATED LIFECYCLE API — main.py:168 `@app.on_event("startup")`; starlette 1.6.0 (the lock) removed Router.on_event entirely and fastapi 0.141.1 only keeps it through a `_DefaultLifespan` shim marked `# ty: ignore[deprecated]`, and that shim is used ONLY when no custom `lifespan=` is passed to `FastAPI(...)`. main.py:67 passes none today, so the executor IS installed — but the day anyone adds a `lifespan=` for any reason, the 40-thread bound silently reverts to CPython's host-dependent `min(32, cpu+4)` with no error.
findings.repro: (a) `grep -rn 'fire_and_forget(' app/ | grep -v 'def ' | wc -l` -> 41. (b) `grep -rn 'on_event\|lifespan' app/ --include=*.py` -> 1 hit, main.py:168. (c) the route enumeration script over app/api/*.py: 78 route decorators, 0 sync handlers, 3 sync dependencies. (e) `pip download starlette==1.6.0 fastapi==0.141.1 --no-deps` then grep the wheels: starlette/routing.py has 0 occurrences of `def on_event`/`add_event_handler`/`on_startup`; fastapi/routing.py has 15 occurrences of `on_startup` and its own `_DefaultLifespan`, selected only `if lifespan is None`.
findings.impact: Individually minor, collectively they are the reason the concurrency model is hard to reason about: (a) makes the loop's real offered load larger than the request count suggests and is the amplifier behind findings 01/04; (b) turns every deploy into a small burst of abandoned upstream work and leaked sockets; (c) is a 40-thread resource nobody has counted; (e) is a latent trap that would silently un-do M13-34 — the single most load-bearing concurrency bound in the service — with no test and no log to catch it.
findings.fix: (a) Route `fire_and_forget` through a module-level `asyncio.Semaphore(BACKGROUND_TASK_CONCURRENCY, default 16)` and add a gauge of in-flight background tasks to the existing stage-timing block, so background work becomes visible and bounded; keep the done-callback logging (#68 wants it in Sentry). (b) Add an `@app.on_event("shutdown")` that calls `executor.shutdown(wait=True, cancel_futures=True)` on the executor returned by `install_default_executor` (store it on `app.state`) and closes the memoised clients. (c) Note the anyio pool in executor.py's docstring and, if any sync dependency ever grows real work, set `anyio.to_thread.current_default_thread_limiter().total_tokens` explicitly at startup. (d) Prune `_next_slot_at` in finding 07's change. (e) Add tests/test_startup_wiring.py::test_default_executor_is_actually_installed — boot the app through `TestClient` and assert `asyncio.get_running_loop()._default_executor._max_workers == default_executor_size()` and that the thread name prefix is `qaren-worker`; that one test converts a silent revert into a red build. Prefer migrating main.py:168 to the modern `lifespan=` context manager in the same change, since the shim is already deprecated in the locked FastAPI.
findings.test_first: tests/test_startup_wiring.py::test_default_executor_is_actually_installed (see (e) above) is the highest-value one and is red only under a future regression; tests/test_background_tasks.py::test_fire_and_forget_is_bounded — spawn 100 fire-and-forget coroutines that block on an event and assert no more than BACKGROUND_TASK_CONCURRENCY are running. Red today.
findings.dedupe: new for (a)-(e) as stated; (a) is adjacent to known:#68 (fire-and-forget failures -> Sentry, still-open) which covers the logging, not the boundedness.

findings.title: MEASURED: the concurrency quality cliff starts at 2 in-flight compares, not 3-4 - success 69%->37%, timeouts 5.5%->50% under a within-query control
findings.evidence: Sweep-line over 2,050 real search_logs intervals. Overlap buckets: 1 -> n=1892 succ 76% p50 19.9s p95 30.0s timeout 5.9%; 2 -> n=68 succ 54% p50 23.7s p95 61.4s timeout 23.5%; 3 -> n=72 succ 38% p50 26.6s p95 58.4s timeout 59.7%; 5+ -> n=18 succ 0% timeout 100%. WITHIN-QUERY paired control over the 32 query strings that appear in BOTH conditions: alone n=941 succ 69.3% p50 18.0s p95 30.0s timeout 5.5% | overlapped n=123 succ 36.6% p50 26.5s p95 59.2s timeout 50.4%. 30 of 32 individual queries degrade. share of rows >35s: overlap1 0.7%, overlap2 23.5%.
findings.repro: python <scratchpad>/m22-review/ls/an5.py and an8.py against <scratchpad>/m22-review/ls/sl.json (13,237 rows pulled read-only: supabase.table('search_logs').select(...).gte('created_at','2026-06-01').range(...)); MEASURED_NUMBERS.txt sections 5 and 12.
findings.impact: This is the first MEASURED concurrency number the project has. M18 modelled the cliff at 3-4 concurrent; measurement puts material degradation at 2 and near-total failure at 3 (60% of requests hard-timeout). The deployment-wide ~10 compares/min ceiling M18 derived is therefore optimistic: at a 20s p50, 10 arrivals/min already means ~3.3 average in flight, i.e. inside the measured 38%-success band. Nine separate episodes across 2 months and 57 distinct queries reproduce it, so it is not one bad night.
findings.fix: Treat 1 concurrent compare as the shipped capacity until offloads are ACTIVE. Concretely: (a) land #71/#73 (Redis/Supabase off the loop, pooled httpx) and #70 (curl pool + fan-out cap) before touching the limiter key in #114 - the ordering rule from M18 is now measured-backed, not modelled; (b) add an explicit in-flight-compare semaphore in the orchestrator entry (structured_comparison_service.py:4609 region) with a fast 503 + Retry-After when it is full, so the 2nd and 3rd concurrent user get an honest 'busy' instead of a 30s timeout that still burns a full LLM fan-out; ship it behind ENABLE_COMPARE_ADMISSION_CONTROL defaulted OFF and flip it after a canary; (c) re-run the overlap sweep after each offload lands - the query is now a one-liner.

findings.impact: The eval gate grades a system its own fan-out is degrading. A nightly eval that reports a low pass rate cannot be distinguished from a genuine quality regression, and a fix that improves quality can be masked by the self-inflicted 60% timeout rate. It also means every historical eval score taken at the default concurrency is a measurement of the SUT under 3-way contention, not of the product a single user sees. Cost side: those timeouts also book $0 (finding 05), so the eval's spend line is fiction too.
findings.fix: Set DEFAULT_CONCURRENCY = 1 in scripts/eval_runner.py:101 and make >1 an explicit opt-in that prints a warning naming the measured cliff; separately, have cron_eval_nightly.py pass concurrency=1 explicitly so the scheduled run is pinned regardless of the module default. findings.evidence: Railway web STREAM_HARD_CAP_SECONDS=30 (baseline/railway-web-vars.txt). MEASURED durations >35,000 ms: 40 rows across 9 dates - 2026-06-02 (1), 06-08 (3), 06-10 (24), 06-11 (6), 06-12 (1), 06-13 (2), 06-15 (1), 06-18 (1), 07-06 (1); 12 rows >=60,000 ms; max 103,697 ms on a SUCCESSFUL text compare (2026-06-02T14:33:45Z, cost $0.006). 36 of the 40 are input_type='text' (the non-stream POST/GET routes at text_routes.py:173-224 / :336-381, which compute duration_ms but enforce no cap) and 4 are camera (image_routes.py:81-248, also uncapped): 57.6s, 72.9s, 35.1s, 37.0s. findings.impact: A user on the non-stream path can wait 60-104 s with no server-side abort; on a single-worker uvicorn that request also holds the loop against everyone else (finding 01's p95 doubling to 59s at overlap 2-3 is the same phenomenon). The 30s figure quoted as 'the cap' in every load discussion is true only for /text/compare/stream. The camera path is the worst case: uncapped AND, per finding 03, its overrun is recorded as a success.

findings.title: MEASURED refutation: the 'Still gathering prices' partial rate is 0.73% on real traffic, not 9.7% - the executor-starvation signature is hard TIMEOUT, not partials
findings.evidence: 'Still gathering prices - give it another tap in a moment.' appears on 1,288 of 13,237 rows (9.73%) BUT 1,251 of those (97%) are duration_ms=0 harness rows; on the 2,050 real rows it is 15 rows = 0.73%. Cross-tabbed against overlap on real rows the partial rate is 1.4% at overlap 1 and 0.0% at overlaps 2, 3, 4 and 6+, while the TIMEOUT message ('We couldn't finish this comparison in time') goes 5.9% -> 23.5% -> 59.7% -> 100%. The 2026-06-08T23:24Z max-overlap window is 12 requests started 1-2s apart across 12 DIFFERENT queries, all 12 ending in TIMEOUT at 25.0-30.7s, cost $0.00 each.
findings.repro: python <scratchpad>/m22-review/ls/an7.py (MEASURED_NUMBERS.txt section 11, "'Still gathering prices' PARTIAL rate: raw vs real") and an3.py (section 3, concurrency-vs-outcome table).
findings.impact: Corrects two working assumptions at once. (1) The partial/'give it another tap' path is a rare real-traffic event (0.7%), not a 10% product problem - product-quality effort aimed at it is aimed at harness output. (2) The hypothesised executor-starvation signature (partial rate rising with overlap) is FALSIFIED; under contention the system does not degrade gracefully into partials, it blows the timeout and returns nothing, having paid for the full upstream fan-out. That changes what to instrument and what to alert on when traffic arrives.
findings.fix: No code change is required for the refutation itself. The actionable consequence: alert on the TIMEOUT error_message rate, not the partial rate, and make the partial path the DESIRED degradation - i.e. when the admission-control semaphore from finding 01 is added, prefer emitting the already-stashed partial response (self._partial_scoring_result / _partial_build_ctx, scs.py:3430-3480) at the cap rather than the bare timeout error, so a contended request returns real scores instead of nothing.

findings.title: P3 sweep: five measured data-shape facts that bound what any load or launch claim can say
findings.evidence: (a) USER ATTRIBUTION: only 18 of 13,237 rows (0.14%) carry a non-null user_id, across 3 distinct user_id values including NULL - so no per-user rate-limit, cohort or retention analysis is derivable from search_logs, and #72 'rate limits keyed on user' has no historical data to validate against. (b) PRICE CACHE STALENESS: product_prices = 3,945 rows, age p50 84 days / p90 109 / max 150; only 9 rows fresher than 7 days and 20 fresher than 30; 1,689 of 3,945 (42.8%) are source_method='estimated'; 3,766 of 3,945 (95.5%) are region='bahrain' with 35-37 rows each for the other 5 GCC regions - and the warmer is OFF (ENABLE_PRICE_CACHE_WARMER unset, 7 skipped runs in the retained log). NOTE product_prices has NO created_at column - its timestamp is fetched_at, which is why a naive growth query 42703s. (c) PERSISTENCE RATIO: 9,983 successful compares produced 27 comparisons rows, because save_comparison only fires when user_id is present - so the 'recorded outputs' corpus can never grow from anonymous traffic. (d) TRAFFIC GAPS: search_logs has zero rows between 2026-07-13 and 2026-08-16 (5 weeks) and 3 rows since 2026-08-31; user_events 146 rows total with nothing after 2026-07-20; users 18 total, last signup 2026-07-06. (e) BUSY-TIME PROFILE: 96.1% of all busy seconds in the real series had exactly ONE compare in flight (2.3% at 2, 1.4% at 3, 0.2% at >=5) - the system has literally never been exercised above 11 concurrent and has spent essentially all its life at concurrency 1.

findings.impact: Bounds every downstream claim. (a) means #72's design cannot be validated from history. (b) means a cold-start launch serves a price cache whose median row is 84 days old and 43% estimated, in one region - and the warmer that would fix it is off. (c) means the offline scoring corpus stays frozen at 27 rows unless anonymous compares start persisting. (d) means there is no recent baseline of ANY kind: the last real activity is 2026-08-25 and the engine has changed by 59 commits since the last data-producing run. (e) is the headline caveat on findings 01/06: the cliff is real and reproducible, but it is measured over 158 overlapped rows out of 2,050, so the curve above 3 concurrent rests on 18 rows from one episode.
findings.fix: Sequenced, cheapest first: add the source column and user attribution from finding 02 so the next traffic is analysable; flip ENABLE_PRICE_CACHE_WARMER on (price-warmer already has SERPER_LIFETIME_LIMIT=2200 armed) and re-measure the age distribution before any canary, since a launch on 84-day-old estimated prices is a product problem before it is a load problem; make save_comparison persist anonymous compares behind a device-fingerprint key so the recorded-output corpus can grow; and capture a fresh single-concurrency latency baseline the day OpenAI credits return, before the first canary, because the newest usable one is 2026-08-25 and predates M20/M21 entirely.

Then, because a metering gate is not a kill switch for spend on doomed work, add a cheap upstream precondition in serper_service.search_web/search_price_organic: skip the Bright Data fallback entirely when the compare cannot succeed (gate it on a process-level OpenAI-availability latch, or simply set ENABLE_BRIGHTDATA_FALLBACK=false until OpenAI credit is restored). findings.title: A Scrape.do/Firecrawl non-200 outside {429,503,0} never trips the breaker AND bills 5 phantom credits per call - measured live: 20 Scrape.do credits burned across Aug+Sep with an empty circuit:* keyspace
findings.evidence: scrapedo_service.py:152-159 `_parse_request_cost` -> `int(resp.headers.get('Scrape.do-Request-Cost', 5))`, i.e. ANY response lacking that header (a 401 auth rejection, a 403, a 400) is charged the render=true default of 5. structured_comparison_service.py:1709-1713 (at 76ace90): `if cost > 0: record_usage('scrapedo', count=cost)` then `if not html: if status in (429, 503) or status == 0: record_failure('scrapedo')` - 401/402/403/404 are in NEITHER set, so the meter is charged and the breaker is not. Firecrawl at scs:1630-1634 is the same shape (`if status == 200: record_usage('firecrawl')` / failure only on 429|503|0). LIVE Upstash: budget:scrapedo:2026-08='15', budget:scrapedo:2026-09='5' (= 3 and 1 calls x 5), budget:firecrawl:lifetime ABSENT entirely, and KEYS 'circuit:*' -> [] : no breaker state exists for any provider in production.
findings.repro: Static + live-state. Read app/services/scrapedo_service.py:152-159,189-198 and git show 76ace90:app/services/structured_comparison_service.py lines 1625-1635 and 1705-1713. Live: Upstash REST GET budget:scrapedo:2026-08 -> '15', GET budget:scrapedo:2026-09 -> '5', KEYS 'circuit:*' -> []. The SCRAPEDO_API_TOKEN is documented dead (401) since 2026-06-26; I did not re-probe it (HARD RULE 1), so the live 401 rate is inferred, but the classification defect is static-certain.
findings.impact: Two compounding effects on a dead or rejecting provider. (a) Runaway retries: with no breaker trip, every price fan-out on every compare re-dispatches a real HTTPS request to a provider that is guaranteed to fail - permanent latency tax inside the 15s price race, forever, with no cooldown. (b) Poisoned accounting: at 5 phantom credits per dead call, the 900/month Scrape.do budget is consumed by ~180 failed calls - a handful of bursty compares - after which has_budget('scrapedo') goes False and the provider is dark for the rest of the month on entirely fictional spend, while /admin/costs/gauges reports scrapedo_month as legitimately exhausted. The 20 credits already burned in Aug+Sep bought nothing.
findings.fix: Two one-line changes in the scs wrappers, no flag needed (they only ever reduce spend/noise): (1) charge the meter only when a request was actually billed - gate `record_usage('scrapedo', count=cost)` on `status == 200 or status in _BILLED_NON_200` where _BILLED_NON_200 = {400,404,410,429,503} (the set the A7 comment already enumerates), so an auth rejection charges 0; and make `_parse_request_cost` return 0, not 5, when the header is absent on a non-200. (2) widen the breaker's failure set at scs:1712 and scs:1633 from {429,503,0} to also include the auth/payment class {401,402,403} so a dead token or an exhausted account trips the circuit after CB_FAILURE_THRESHOLD=3 and stops re-dispatching for CB_RECOVERY_TIMEOUT.

findings.evidence: brightdata_service.py:238-247 defines `bd_search_shopping` (tbm=shop, Serper-shaped) - grep across app/ finds ZERO call sites; only `bd_search_web` is imported (serper_service.py:629 and :958). serper_service._do_serper_shopping (:771-826) has no fallback branch at all: a non-200 logs SERPER_SHOPPING_NON_200 and `return {}`. The module's own header comment (:1-6) states Bright Data exists as 'a FALLBACK when the Serper key is exhausted/erroring' - which is true for organic and false for shopping.
findings.repro: python scratchpad/probe_bd.py, same run as -01: `await serper_service._do_serper_shopping('iphone 15','bh')` with `_serper_post` returning 403 produced `shopping_result: {}` and `brightdata_dispatched` did not grow (4 entries before and after, all organic). Log line emitted: `SERPER_SHOPPING_NON_200 gl=bh status=403 ... product='iphone 15'`.
findings.impact: Google Shopping is the highest-yield price source in the cascade (search_product_prices -> the shopping[] array feeds the Tier-1 price candidates). Today, under the -50 Serper balance, that tier returns empty on EVERY compare while the organic tiers keep working via Bright Data. The result is not an error the user can see - it is a quieter, worse comparison: fewer price candidates, more Tier-2/Tier-3 estimates, more 'Still gathering prices' (1,288 occurrences already the #1 error string in search_logs). It also means the burst behaviour is asymmetric: the shopping leg fails in ~0.3s while every organic leg now costs up to 9s (see -11), so the pipeline spends its whole wall-clock budget on the legs that fall back and none on the tier that matters most.
findings.fix: Wire the already-written `bd_search_shopping` into `_do_serper_shopping`'s non-200 and exception paths, mirroring search_web's three-branch shape (no-key / budget-out / request-failed), and gate it on `_brightdata_enabled()` so an unset flag is byte-identical. Do this ONLY together with -01's budget gate, otherwise it adds another uncapped Bright Data leg per product per compare. If the gate cannot ship first, the correct interim action is the opposite one: leave shopping unwired and record the coverage loss, because an uncapped new spend path is worse than the missing tier.

findings.title: The first thing a burst shows users is a dead end: the 429 handler drops Retry-After and the client maps code RATE_LIMITED to 'generic' - 'No comparison loaded / Back to history', no retry affordance
findings.evidence: failureClassification.ts:42-56 - the matrix tests USAGE_LIMIT, 404, 401, TIMEOUT/STREAM_TIMEOUT, 503, >=500, and `!err?.response`; a 429 whose code is RATE_LIMITED (not USAGE_LIMIT) matches none and falls to `return 'generic'` at :56. ResultsScreen.tsx:659 `const isTimeout = loadError === 'timeout'` - only 'timeout' gets `results.timeout.retry` + handleRetry; 'generic' renders `results.emptyState.title` = "No comparison loaded" with CTA `results.emptyState.cta` = "Back to history" (src/i18n/en.json:747-748). Server side: app/middleware/error_handler.py:122-128 `rate_limit_handler` returns `_build_error_response(429, 'Rate limit exceeded. Please try again later.', request_id)` - a bare JSONResponse; slowapi's own `_rate_limit_exceeded_handler` sets Retry-After and X-RateLimit-*, and this replacement sets no headers at all.
findings.repro: Static, traced end-to-end at HEAD. app/middleware/error_handler.py:122 -> app/main.py:151 registers it for RateLimitExceeded -> the wire body is {success:false, error:'Rate limit exceeded...', code:'RATE_LIMITED', request_id} with no Retry-After -> SmartCompareApp/src/services/api.ts:146-153 only special-cases data.code==='USAGE_LIMIT' and re-rejects everything else -> classifyLoadFailure(err) with status 429 / code 'RATE_LIMITED' returns 'generic' -> ResultsScreen.tsx:654,659,674-690.
findings.impact: This is the FIRST cell of the burst cascade to engage. /text/compare, /text/compare/stream, /url/compare and /image/identify all carry @limiter.limit('10/minute') keyed on the shared Railway edge-proxy IP (M18 LS-ratelimit-01, still true: ENABLE_PROXY_AWARE_RATELIMIT is absent from the 54 prod vars), so at 50 simultaneous app-opens or >10 compares/min DEPLOYMENT-WIDE, the 11th user onward gets a 429 - and sees a terminal empty state that reads as 'your comparison does not exist', with the only affordance being Back to history. No retry button, no wait hint, and no Retry-After for the client to back off on, so the app and the user both hammer the same bucket. Every other transient failure class in this app (offline, 5xx, 503, timeout) was deliberately routed to the soft retryable state by M18 MB-flows-05; 429 is the one that was missed, and it is the one a launch burst produces.
findings.fix: Two small changes. Server: in error_handler.rate_limit_handler, preserve slowapi's headers - compute the reset from `exc.detail`/the limiter and attach `Retry-After` (and X-RateLimit-Limit/Remaining/Reset) to the JSONResponse, so clients and any CDN can back off. Client: add `if (status === 429) return 'timeout';` to failureClassification.ts immediately after the USAGE_LIMIT branch (USAGE_LIMIT is already matched first at :49, so paywall routing is unaffected), which reuses the existing soft retryable state + handleRetry with zero new copy. Ships un-flagged in the next `eas update --branch preview`; note that phones currently run 97b5f15, so the client half only reaches users with that OTA.
findings.test_first: __tests__/api.networkMatrix.m18.test.ts: `expect(classifyLoadFailure({response:{status:429,data:{code:'RATE_LIMITED'}}})).toBe('timeout')` - RED at HEAD (returns 'generic'). Backend: assert the 429 response from a decorated route carries a Retry-After header - RED at HEAD.
findings.dedupe: known:M18 MB-flows-05 (fixed - the classification matrix landed) - this is the residual cell that fix did not cover; the limiter's shared-bucket key itself is known:M18 LS-ratelimit-01 / #114, still-open by design

findings.title: Every deploy kills in-flight SSE compares and silently burns the freemium credit: no shutdown hook, and the refund is a create_task on the closing loop whose cancellation is swallowed
findings.evidence: app/main.py has exactly one lifecycle hook - `@app.on_event('startup')` at :168 for the executor - and no shutdown handler, no lifespan, no signal handling (grep for on_event|lifespan|shutdown|SIGTERM|timeout_graceful over app/ returns only main.py:168). uvicorn is pinned 0.52.4 (requirements.txt:192) and started as `uvicorn app.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port $PORT` (railway.json + Procfile) with no --timeout-graceful-shutdown; RAILWAY_DEPLOYMENT_DRAINING_SECONDS is absent from all 54 web vars. Streams run up to STREAM_HARD_CAP_SECONDS=30 (Railway prod value; default 25 at scs:1365). The refund path is text_routes.py:685-689 `fire_and_forget(refund_comparison_credit(user_id), label='usage_refund.text_stream.incomplete')`, and app/utils/async_utils.py:54-58 is `asyncio.create_task(coro)` whose done-callback opens with `if t.cancelled(): return` - a cancelled refund logs nothing at all.
findings.repro: Static composition, no destructive test run. Read app/main.py:1-172 (no shutdown hook), git show 76ace90:app/api/text_routes.py:544-691 (the event_generator finally and its three branches at :638/:662/:685), app/utils/async_utils.py:30-67, app/services/usage_service.py:488-505 (refund does a Redis round trip, inline on the loop because ENABLE_ASYNC_REDIS_OFFLOAD is absent from prod vars).
findings.impact: Two distinct losses per deploy, and this repo deploys often (M18 LS-railway-metrics-06 counts ~20 deployments' worth of churn). On SIGKILL the generator's `finally` never runs at all: the reserved daily/monthly credit is gone, no history row is saved, no search_logs row is written - the compare is invisible in every metric AND the user is charged for it. Even on a clean drain the `finally` only *schedules* the refund on a loop that is about to close, so the task is cancelled before its Redis write and `_on_done` returns silently at async_utils.py:57. Either way the user loses a credit from a 3/day free allowance with zero trace anywhere - no log line, no Sentry event, no counter. This is also the one failure mode a burst makes routine, because the more concurrent 30s streams are open, the more credits a single deploy eats.
findings.fix: Two parts, both un-flagged. (1) Make the drain deterministic: add `--timeout-graceful-shutdown 35` to the uvicorn start command in railway.json (one margin above STREAM_HARD_CAP_SECONDS=30) and set RAILWAY_DEPLOYMENT_DRAINING_SECONDS to match, so in-flight streams finish and their `finally` actually runs instead of being SIGKILLed mid-yield. (2) Make the refund survive the loop: in the SSE finally, `await` the refund instead of fire-and-forgetting it (it is the last statement of a generator that is already ending, so it costs no user-visible latency), or - if a shutdown-only shield is preferred - wrap it in asyncio.shield. Separately, change async_utils._on_done to log a WARNING on `t.cancelled()` rather than returning, so a lost refund is at least visible.
findings.test_first: Drive text_compare_stream's event_generator with an orchestrator stub that yields two status events then raises CancelledError, with a spy on refund_comparison_credit; assert the refund coroutine was AWAITED to completion (not merely scheduled) before the generator finished. RED at HEAD - the spy sees a Task that never runs when the loop is closed immediately after.

findings.impact: Quantified request multiplication under a 429 storm. Per LLM call the SDK default is 3 attempts; the verdict chain then adds a second-model fallback with its own 3 (extraction_service.py:2482-2487), so one verdict can be 6 upstream requests - exactly double what the launch runbook sizes for. Measured today, with OpenAI at insufficient_quota, that amplification is what turns a doomed compare into a 23-second one: search_logs 2026-09-02 shows a 'Could not identify two products' failure that took 22,995 ms, i.e. the product-identification call alone burned its full retry ladder with SDK backoff before giving up. The url_extraction gap means that even after the operator sets OPENAI_MAX_RETRIES=1, the /url/compare path keeps its 3 attempts, so the knob will appear to under-deliver and the URL path stays the loudest 429 amplifier.
findings.fix: One line: pass `max_retries=openai_max_retries()` in url_extraction_service.get_client() (import it locally the way extraction_service.py:48 does, to keep the module's import graph unchanged). Separately, set the runbook's launch values on both Railway services now - OPENAI_MAX_RETRIES=1 and OPENAI_FALLBACK_MAX_RETRIES=0 - which drops verdict_chain_max_attempts() from 6 to 3; both are read fresh at client construction / per fallback call, so only the module-level openai_service.client needs a restart to pick them up (documented at model_config.py:156-160).
findings.test_first: assert url_extraction_service.get_client().max_retries == model_config.openai_max_retries() with OPENAI_MAX_RETRIES=1 monkeypatched - RED at HEAD (returns the SDK default 2). Plus a config test asserting verdict_chain_max_attempts() == 3 under the runbook env.
findings.dedupe: known:M18 LS-capacity-math-03 (429 storm triples request volume) - still-open, and this is the unreported residual: #117's knob has a hole in it and was never applied to prod

findings.title: Cost accounting omits every scraping provider: total_cost counts only OpenAI tokens and $0.001/Serper-call, so search_logs.cost and /admin/costs read 0.0 on runs that actually spent Bright Data requests
findings.evidence: There are exactly three mutations of self.total_cost at 76ace90: `_track_gpt_cost` (scs:7973-7979, prompt*0.15/1M + completion*0.60/1M), `_track_serper_cost` (scs:7982-7986, flat += 0.001), and `_track_cost_amount` (scs:7988-7990, used only at scs:6631/6674 for the Tier-1.5 cascade). Bright Data, Firecrawl, Scrape.do, Zyte and Algolia never appear. That value is what database_service.log_search(cost=...) persists (text_routes.py:271,420,641 pass `result['metadata']['total_cost']`) and what admin_routes.costs_api sums into `openai_paid_usd` (admin_routes.py:731-746). MEASURED: the three 2026-09-02 search_logs rows all carry cost=0.0 with durations 22,995 / 2,554 / 31,008 ms - runs long enough to have driven the full organic fan-out through Bright Data (see -01).
findings.repro: grep for total_cost mutations in git show 76ace90:app/services/structured_comparison_service.py -> 3 sites; read database_service.log_search:464-507 and admin_routes.py:714-777. Supabase SELECT * FROM search_logs WHERE created_at >= '2026-08-20' ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 40 -> the three 2026-09-02 rows, all cost 0.0, success false.
findings.impact: The cost column is the only per-request spend series this product has (16,283 rows) and it is structurally blind to the providers that are actually spending right now. Concretely: 2026-06's cost_sum of $20.53 over 9,157 rows is an OpenAI+Serper figure with every render and every SERP-proxy request missing; 2026-09's $0.000 over 3 rows reads as 'free' for compares that dispatched Bright Data. Any unit-economics decision, any MAX_MONTHLY_COST-style guard, and the /admin/costs dashboard all inherit the same blindness - and they inherit it in precisely the regime where scraping is the dominant cost, because OpenAI is dead and Serper 403s for free.
findings.fix: Give the three scraping wrappers a cost hook the way Serper already has one: add `_track_cost_amount(<unit>)` calls in scs._firecrawl_scraper (next to record_usage at :1631), scs._scrapedo_scraper (next to :1710, scaled by the billed `cost` credits), and a `track_cost_fn` passthrough into brightdata_service.bd_search_web so a dispatched SERP request lands in total_cost too. Units belong in one module-level table next to the existing 0.001 Serper constant so they are auditable in one place. This is additive to a number that is already written to every row; no flag needed, and it makes -09's dead MAX_MONTHLY_COST cap meaningful for the first time.
findings.test_first: Run a compare through the orchestrator with the Serper post stubbed to 403 and _bd_post stubbed, then assert `result['metadata']['total_cost'] > 0` and that it includes a brightdata component. RED at HEAD (0.0).
findings.dedupe: known:#66 (admin cost meters wrong) - still-open; #66 is about the admin surface, this pins the upstream cause (total_cost itself has no scraper inputs) with fresh measured rows

findings.title: Budget meters count SUCCESS only, so provider DEATH is the one state they cannot show: prod Redis has an empty circuit:* keyspace, no firecrawl counter at all, and a Serper gauge frozen at 899/2200 while every call 403s
findings.evidence: serper_service.py:658-660 - `response.raise_for_status()` then `await _record_usage_async('serper')`: a 403 raises before the meter. scs:1630 - `if status == 200: record_usage('firecrawl')`. api_budget_service._maybe_fire_burn_alert (:419-457) is reachable ONLY from record_usage (:463-489), so the single Sentry spend alert in the system is downstream of success too. LIVE Upstash: KEYS 'circuit:*' -> [] (no breaker state has ever been written for ANY provider); KEYS 'budget:*' -> only scrapedo:2026-08/09 and three serper lifetime keys - `budget:firecrawl:lifetime` does not exist; GET budget:serper:f47c159b:lifetime -> '899' against a 2200 ceiling. admin_routes.py:864-871 renders exactly those numbers as `serper_lifetime` 899/2200 (41%) and `firecrawl_lifetime` 0/450 (0%).
findings.repro: Upstash REST (read-only): KEYS 'budget:*', KEYS 'circuit:*', KEYS 'cost:*', GET on each. Cross-read app/services/serper_service.py:645-668, git show 76ace90:app/services/structured_comparison_service.py:1625-1635, app/services/api_budget_service.py:419-489,665-700, app/api/admin_routes.py:837-871.
findings.impact: This is the answer to 'what would tell an operator the loop is saturated or the money is leaking': nothing on this dashboard can. A depleted Serper key stops incrementing, so the gauge FREEZES at 41% headroom rather than alarming - the meter's reading is identical for 'plenty of credit' and 'every call is a 403'. Firecrawl has never metered a single 200 in this deployment's Redis history, so its gauge is a permanent 0/450 and its 80%-burn alert can never fire. And the empty circuit:* keyspace proves no breaker has ever engaged for any provider, which is consistent with -02: the failure classes that actually occur (401/403/depletion) are all outside the {429,503,0} trip set. Meanwhile the one provider that IS spending (Bright Data) has no gauge on /costs/gauges at all, even though get_usage_summary() emits a brightdata row that will read 0 forever.
findings.fix: Meter DISPATCH, not success. Add a `record_attempt(provider)` counter incremented before every outbound provider call and surface `attempts` alongside `used` in get_usage_summary/costs_gauges, so a 403'd provider shows attempts climbing with used flat - the exact signature of depletion. Add a `brightdata` gauge to admin_routes.costs_gauges (get_usage_summary already returns the row). Finally, add the auth/payment class to the breaker's failure set as -02 describes, so `circuit:*` stops being empty and the dashboard's breaker column carries information. All additive; no behaviour flag required.
findings.test_first: With _serper_post stubbed to 403, call search_web 3 times and assert get_usage_summary()['providers']['serper']['attempts'] == 3 while ['used'] == 0. RED at HEAD (there is no attempts field, and a depleted provider is indistinguishable from an idle one).
findings.dedupe: known:#80 (cron failure visibility) and #66 - both still-open; the success-only metering root cause and the empty-circuit:*/absent-firecrawl-counter live evidence are new

findings.title: MAX_MONTHLY_COST and FREE_TIER_DAILY_LIMIT are set on Railway prod but read only by two zero-caller functions - prod Redis has an empty cost:* keyspace, so the operator's spend cap has never been consulted once
findings.evidence: cache_service.py:712 `MAX_MONTHLY_COST = float(os.getenv('MAX_MONTHLY_COST', '100'))` is read only by `check_monthly_budget` (:730-739); cache_service.py:665 `FREE_TIER_DAILY_LIMIT = int(os.getenv('FREE_TIER_DAILY_LIMIT','5'))` only by `check_rate_limit` (:668-686). grep for `check_rate_limit|check_monthly_budget|track_api_cost|add_api_cost` across app/ returns ONLY their own definitions - zero callers. Both names ARE present in the live Railway variable list for `web` and `price-warmer`. LIVE Upstash: KEYS 'cost:*' -> [] - the `cost:<YYYY-MM>` key `add_api_cost` would write has never existed.
findings.repro: Grep app/ for the four symbol names (definitions only). Upstash REST KEYS 'cost:*' -> []. Cross-check against baseline/railway-web-vars.txt, which lists MAX_MONTHLY_COST and FREE_TIER_DAILY_LIMIT among the 54 live `web` vars.
findings.impact: An operator has configured what reads like the system's spend ceiling and its freemium ceiling, and neither is wired to anything - the live daily limit is usage_service.TIER_LIMITS (free = 3), and there is no monthly cost cap at all. That false safety is what makes finding -01 dangerous rather than merely untidy: the person who set MAX_MONTHLY_COST reasonably believes Bright Data spend is bounded. It is not, by this or by anything else. The empty cost:* keyspace is the proof that no code has ever attempted to enforce it.
findings.fix: Pick one and do it explicitly. Either delete the four dead symbols and the two constants (M13's own recommendation) and remove both vars from Railway so nobody trusts them again; or - better, given -01 - make MAX_MONTHLY_COST real by calling `add_api_cost(total_cost)` once per compare in the response-build path and consulting `check_monthly_budget()` at the compare gate, which only becomes meaningful once -07 puts scraper spend into total_cost. Do not leave the current third state, where the knob exists in prod and does nothing.
findings.test_first: A config test asserting that every non-secret Railway variable name is read by at least one reachable code path - or, minimally, `assert check_monthly_budget.__module__ callers != []`. Either is RED at HEAD.
findings.dedupe: known:M13 data-06 (P2->P3, 'check_rate_limit/FREE_TIER_DAILY_LIMIT has zero callers anywhere') - still-open, re-raised to P2 because the live-config evidence (both vars SET on prod, cost:* empty) is new and it interacts with -01

findings.title: DEBUG_STAGE_TIMINGS=true on BOTH prod services falsifies six in-code 'zero overhead / true no-op in prod' contracts, and ships internal per-stage timings to every client and into comparisons.full_response
findings.evidence: Railway `web` AND `price-warmer` both set DEBUG_STAGE_TIMINGS=true. The code says otherwise in six places: response_builder.py:23-25 'gated on DEBUG_STAGE_TIMINGS=true so the factual_verdict None-emit hook adds zero overhead in production'; extraction_service.py:28; firecrawl_service.py:109; scrapedo_service.py:34; scs:7185 'no-op in prod (reuses the DEBUG_STAGE_TIMINGS pattern)'; scs:5841. Functionally, scs:951-964 caches the flag at first read, scs:4419 `stage_timings = {} if _debug_timings_enabled() else None` turns instrumentation on, and scs:3595 / scs:4345 then do `result.setdefault('metadata',{})['stage_timings_ms'] = orchestrator_timings` - so per-stage timings including a `per_product` array go out in the response body and are persisted into comparisons.full_response.
findings.repro: Static + live config. `railway variables --service web --kv` (captured in baseline/railway-web-vars.txt) shows DEBUG_STAGE_TIMINGS=true for both services; read git show 76ace90:app/services/structured_comparison_service.py lines 951-964, 4419, 3595, 4345, and the five sibling flag readers.
findings.impact: Three costs, all paid on every compare and multiplied by a burst. (a) The comments are wrong, so any future reviewer reasoning about production overhead from the source will reason from a false premise - the same 'docs-as-wrong-truth' class M13 named. (b) Payload and storage bloat: an internal timing dict per compare on the wire and in every comparisons row, growing the response the SSE path must serialise inside the 30s cap. (c) Diagnostic log volume: the flag also unlocks the pros/cons raw-response dump (truncated to 2000 chars per compare, extraction_service.py:28-37) and the firecrawl/scrapedo PRICE_PIPELINE_DIAG invocation lines, each of which does a Redis-backed get_remaining()/get_breaker_state() read at call time - blocking work on the single event loop, per provider attempt, per product.
findings.fix: Set DEBUG_STAGE_TIMINGS=false on both Railway services (one variable, restores every gated block to the no-op its comments claim). If per-stage timings are genuinely wanted in prod, split the flag: keep an internal STAGE_TIMINGS_LOG that only logs, and never attach `metadata.stage_timings_ms` to a client response - the current single flag conflates 'instrument' with 'publish to users and persist forever'.
findings.test_first: With DEBUG_STAGE_TIMINGS=true, assert the compare response's `metadata` does NOT contain `stage_timings_ms` (i.e. publication is gated separately from instrumentation). RED at HEAD. Plus a config test that the diagnostic flag is absent/false in the prod variable set.
findings.dedupe: new

findings.title: The binding capacity constraint is no longer the limiter: the Bright Data fallback turns each ~0.3s Serper 403 into a 9s Google-proxy fetch, and measured wall clock went from p90 = 1 ms (Aug) to 22,995-31,008 ms (Sep)
findings.evidence: brightdata_service.py:44-47 `_TIMEOUT = adapter_timeout(20.0)`; adapter_timeouts.py:41-44,47-57 compute `max(1.0, min(10.0, PRICE_RACE_TIMEOUT=15.0) - 1.0)` = 9.0 - confirmed 9.0 at runtime by the probe. The module header (:13-15) says each request proxies a live `google.com/search` fetch. MEASURED search_logs: 2026-08 n=714, p90=1 ms, p95=3 ms, max=4,337 ms; 2026-09 n=3, p50=22,995 ms, p90/max=31,008 ms - and the 31,008 ms row is the STREAM_HARD_CAP_SECONDS=30 ceiling (scs:1365, enforced at scs:3080/3894) plus overhead, i.e. the compare was cut off, not completed.
findings.repro: Supabase SELECT over search_logs (baseline/search_logs_summary.txt plus my own SELECT of the 40 newest rows). probe_bd.json reports `bd_timeout_s: 9.0` from the real module. Read adapter_timeouts.py:1-57 and git show 76ace90:app/services/structured_comparison_service.py:1365,3080,3894.
findings.impact: This reorders the whole cascade that M18 modelled. With one uvicorn worker on one event loop and the offload flags still OFF in prod (ENABLE_SYNC_DB_OFFLOAD and ENABLE_ASYNC_REDIS_OFFLOAD are absent from all 54 web vars), a compare that now occupies ~23-30s of wall clock rather than ~2-4s means throughput collapses far below the 10/min shared-bucket ceiling - so under a burst users hit the 30s hard cap and the 'Comparison data was incomplete' / 'Still gathering prices' terminals BEFORE they ever hit a 429. The limiter that #114 holds open specifically because it protects the loop is no longer the thing that engages first; the provider-substitution latency is. Any activation-order decision that still assumes '10 compares/min is the wall' is sizing against the wrong constraint while Serper is dead.
findings.fix: Nothing to change in the timeout itself - 9.0s is correctly clamped under the 10s per-source wrap and the 15s race. The fix is upstream and is the same lever as -01: while OpenAI is dead, turn ENABLE_BRIGHTDATA_FALLBACK off so the legs fail fast at the 403 instead of buying a 9s proxy fetch each; when OpenAI is restored, arm ENABLE_BRIGHTDATA_BUDGET_GATE first so the fallback is bounded, and re-derive the compares/min ceiling from measured wall clock (not from the limiter) before re-keying the limiter per #114. Record the new number in the capacity doc so the ordering rule is re-stated against the current provider mix.
findings.test_first: A capacity regression test that runs one compare through the orchestrator with _serper_post stubbed 403 and _bd_post stubbed to sleep 3s, and asserts total wall clock stays under a declared budget - it should fail loudly when a provider substitution multiplies per-leg latency. Nothing pins this today.
findings.dedupe: known:M18 LS-capacity-math-01 / LS-railway-metrics-01 (deployment-wide ~10 compares/min is the binding ceiling) - regressed/superseded under the current provider state; the 9s-per-leg substitution and the Aug->Sep latency series are new

findings.title: Nothing detects a wedged or saturated loop: /health does no I/O, Railway's healthcheck is a deploy gate (so the ON_FAILURE budget is never consumed by a stall), Sentry captures only 5xx, and every provider failure is a bare logger.warning
findings.evidence: railway.json:6-10 - `healthcheckPath: /health`, `healthcheckTimeout: 30`, `restartPolicyType: ON_FAILURE`, `restartPolicyMaxRetries: 3`. app/main.py:307-313 - /health returns a static dict with zero I/O, so it cannot observe Redis, Supabase, the executor queue or provider state; and being on the same single loop it either answers instantly or not at all. sentry_service.py:214-233 - `_captured_5xx = frozenset(range(500,600)) - {503}` with traces_sample_rate=0.1; a 429, a Serper 403, a Bright Data dispatch and a Scrape.do 401 are none of them exceptions or 5xx, so none reach Sentry. app/utils/async_utils.py:56-64 - the fire-and-forget done-callback logs `logger.warning('fire-and-forget %s failed: %r', ...)` and never calls sentry_sdk.capture_exception, and returns silently on `t.cancelled()` at :57-58.
findings.repro: Static. Read railway.json in full, app/main.py:301-318, app/services/sentry_service.py:197-238, app/utils/async_utils.py:30-67. The Railway-side semantics (healthcheckPath gates a DEPLOYMENT's promotion rather than running as a continuous liveness probe, so ON_FAILURE/maxRetries counts process EXITS) is inferred from Railway's documented behaviour, not verified against their API - hence the 0.75 confidence.
findings.impact: Answers the lane's cascade question with 'nothing engages'. A stalled event loop does not exit, so the ON_FAILURE budget of 3 is never spent and the 4th-failure scenario never arrives - the service simply stops serving with 1 replica and no auto-recovery, and because /health does no I/O there is no probe that could notice. The one alerting channel that exists (Sentry) is deaf to the entire burst cascade: 429s, provider 403/401s, budget exhaustion, and every fire-and-forget failure - which is precisely the set of events that constitute this system's failure modes. #68 is still open at HEAD and this is why it matters: under load the refunds, history saves and analytics writes that get cancelled or fail are the ONLY record that a user was charged for work they never received, and their failures are a WARNING line in a per-deployment log that Railway discards on the next deploy.
findings.fix: Three additive steps, none behaviour-changing. (1) Close #68: add `sentry_sdk.capture_exception(exc)` to async_utils._on_done alongside the WARNING, and log (do not silently return) on `t.cancelled()`. (2) Give /health a cheap dependency-aware sibling - /ready that does one Redis PING and one Supabase count with a hard 2s budget - and point Railway's healthcheckPath at it, so a wedged dependency is at least visible to a deploy and to an external prober; keep /health as the no-I/O liveness endpoint. (3) Route the provider-failure class to Sentry: promote the Serper 403 / Bright Data non-200 / Scrape.do-Firecrawl auth-class paths from logger.warning to a rate-limited sentry_sdk.capture_message, reusing the one-shot sentinel pattern already in _maybe_fire_burn_alert so a burst does not flood the stream.
findings.test_first: Assert that a fire-and-forget coroutine which raises causes sentry_sdk.capture_exception to be called (RED at HEAD - only a logger.warning fires), and that a cancelled task emits a log line (RED - async_utils.py:57 returns silently).
findings.dedupe: known:#68 (fire-and-forget failures -> Sentry) still-open; known:#81 (/health probes) still-open; known:M18 LS-railway-metrics-03 (zero-HA + hard restart budget) still-open - with the refinement that a stalled loop never consumes the restart budget at all, so 'what happens on the 4th failure' is moot; known:M18 LS-event-loop-09 still-open

findings.title: P3 sweep: five latent cost/failure-mode defects around the provider fallback and refund paths
findings.evidence: (a) serper_service.py:75-81 `_SERPER_EXHAUSTED_PREFIX='serper:exhausted:'`, `_SERPER_EXHAUSTED_TTL = 6*3600` - the per-key depletion flag EXPIRES after 6h, so with a permanently negative account the multi-key rotation loop (:491 `max_attempts = max(1, len(keys))`, both SERPER_API_KEY and SERPER_API_KEYS are set in prod) re-dispatches a full 403 storm across every key on every search leg, every 6 hours, forever; depletion is never durably learned. Live Upstash KEYS 'serper*' -> [] confirms the flags have already expired since the 2026-09-02 traffic. (b) brightdata_service.py:238-247 `bd_search_shopping` has zero callers - dead code carrying a maintained defensive mapper (see -03). (c) brightdata_service.py:84-97 `_bd_record`'s docstring says 'Meter every DISPATCHED Bright Data request (it bills per request regardless of hit)' but returns at :87-88 when the gate is off, which is prod - the comment describes behaviour that does not ship. (d) app/api/text_routes.py:247, 400, 673, 687 all call `refund_comparison_credit(user_id)` with no `consumed_keys`, so the M18 usage-symmetry parameter (usage_service.py:488-496, 'pass the gate result's consumed_keys to credit the exact window the consume debited') is unwired at all four route call sites - only usage_service.py:135's anon helper forwards it, and that helper is itself unwired per #128. Every refund therefore takes the legacy floor-at-zero + previous-window fallback (_refund_credit_sync:472-486), which at a UTC midnight boundary credits back the NEW day's counter when it holds any debit - a free extra compare today and an over-count yesterday. (e) scs:1365 `STREAM_HARD_CAP_SECONDS = float(os.getenv(...))` is evaluated at module import, so the prod value of 30 cannot be changed without a redeploy, unlike the ~30 other flags in this tree that are deliberately read per call.
findings.repro: Static reads at HEAD 76ace90 for (b)(c)(e) and via git show 76ace90:app/api/text_routes.py for (d) (line numbers identical to the worktree). (a) additionally confirmed live: Upstash REST KEYS 'serper*' and KEYS '*exhaust*' both return [] despite the 2026-09-02 403 traffic, i.e. the 6h TTL has already reset the rotation state.
findings.impact: Individually minor; together they are the long tail of the same theme as -01/-02: the fallback machinery meters and remembers less than its comments claim. (a) costs a bounded but recurring burst of doomed Serper POSTs (legs x keys, every 6h) and keeps the rotation logs noisy. (d) is a small freemium-accounting drift that only shows at window boundaries but is systematic under a burst spanning UTC midnight. (c) and (b) are documentation/dead-code debt that will mislead the next reader of exactly the module finding -01 asks an operator to change.
findings.fix: (a) Distinguish a transient failure from a hard depletion signal: when `_response_signals_exhaustion` sees 402/403 (serper_service.py:193), write the flag with no TTL (the burn-alert sentinel at api_budget_service.py:452-455 already uses exactly this lifetime-vs-monthly ternary) and clear it on key rotation. (b) Either wire bd_search_shopping per -03 or delete it. (c) Reword the _bd_record docstring to state that metering only happens with the gate on. (d) Thread `usage_check['consumed_keys']` from the gate into all four refund_comparison_credit calls in text_routes.py - the parameter already exists and is already tested. (e) Move STREAM_HARD_CAP_SECONDS behind a per-call accessor like every other knob in this module.
findings.test_first: (a) After a 403, assert the Redis exhaustion flag has no TTL. (d) Assert text_routes' refund passes the gate's consumed_keys through - RED at all four sites. (e) Assert monkeypatching STREAM_HARD_CAP_SECONDS in os.environ changes the enforced cap without a module reload - RED at HEAD.
findings.dedupe: new (item (d) touches known:#128, which is about the anon-gate refund wiring, not the four authed route call sites)

findings.title: MEASURED: Upstash REST RTT from the prod container is 178 ms and both offload flags are UNSET, so every cache HIT blocks the single event loop for a full round trip

Container env: ENABLE_SYNC_DB_OFFLOAD=<UNSET>, ENABLE_ASYNC_REDIS_OFFLOAD=<UNSET>. cache_service.py:541: 'The module-level redis_client is a BLOCKING (httpx.Client) client'.

findings.impact: M18 listed 'Upstash RTT from Railway NEVER measured' as the biggest unknown in the load model; it is 178 ms (median, min 176, max 197) and Supabase is ~285 ms (max 884 cold). Per the M18 ordering rule the offloads must be ACTIVE and hop-count-verified BEFORE the #114 limiter key changes. Do it as two separate deploys with the /health probe and a stage-timing capture between them so the specs_ms/reviews_ms floor can be re-measured; if the floor drops off the 160-210 ms band the offload is genuinely live.

findings.title: MEASURED concurrency cliff is at TWO in-flight compares, not the modelled 3-4: success falls 76%->54%->38%->0% and timeouts rise 5.9%->23.5%->59.7%->100%
findings.evidence: Interval overlap over the 2,050 real rows (d>=1000 ms): MAX in-flight=11; overlap=1 n=1892 succ 76% p50 19,927 ms p95 30,004 timeout 5.9% | overlap=2 n=68 succ 54% p50 23,885 p95 61,355 timeout 23.5% | overlap=3 n=72 succ 38% p50 26,669 timeout 59.7% | overlap>=4 n=18 succ 0% timeout 100%. executor.py:16 docstring: '40 leaves headroom for ~2 concurrent full fan-outs'.
findings.repro: The recomputation is scratchpad/m22-review/ls2/VERIFY.txt (independent re-derivation of the same result the lane's part-1 file reports). Source rows: scratchpad/m22-review/ls/sl.json (13,237 read-only SELECTed rows). Confounder control included: over the 32 query strings that appear BOTH alone and overlapped, alone n=941 succ 69.3% p50 18.0 s vs overlapped n=123 succ 36.6% p50 26.5 s, so it is not query mix.
findings.impact: This is the first measured concurrency number the project has - M18's '3-4' was modelled. It is worse than modelled AND it is a DEADLINE cliff, not a capacity cliff: single-request p50 is 19.9 s against a 30 s hard cap (only 10 s of headroom) and single-request p95 is already 30.0 s, i.e. AT the cap. A second concurrent compare adds 4-7 s to p50, which is enough to push the majority over. Loop-blocking (finding 01) does not saturate until roughly 60 compares/min, so the binding constraints in order are (a) the 30 s deadline vs a 20 s median, (b) the shared-IP 10/minute limiter, (c) OpenAI TPM. Any launch plan that assumes 3 concurrent users are safe is wrong by one user.
findings.fix: Do not raise concurrency; cut the median. The measured budget says where: verdict is 20-70% of total (median 5.8 s) and price_ms reaches the 15 s _PRICE_RACE_TIMEOUT on cold legs, while scoring and response-build are ~0.5 ms. Land the offloads (finding 01) to recover ~1 s, then either lower _PRICE_RACE_TIMEOUT or make the verdict streaming-first so a partial lands before the cap. Until median wall drops below ~12 s, treat 1 concurrent compare as the supported ceiling and say so in the launch runbook. Re-measure this exact table after each change - it is now a repeatable gate.
findings.test_first: A harness test (offline, fake OpenAI with a 20 s scripted delay) that runs 2 compares concurrently through the real route and asserts both complete inside STREAM_HARD_CAP_SECONDS - red today.
findings.dedupe: known:M18 load answer - status regressed relative to the model (M18 modelled a 3-4 cliff and all-modelled concurrency; measured is 2, with n=68/72/18 in the overlapped buckets)

findings.title: The 30 s stream hard cap does not bound the tail (ENABLE_FULL_STREAM_DEADLINE default OFF): 40 measured requests ran past 35 s, 12 past 60 s, max 103.7 s against a 120 s client timeout
findings.evidence: scs:1361-1364 'ENABLE_FULL_STREAM_DEADLINE (default OFF) extends this cap over that tail ... Flag OFF -> the tail is unbounded, exactly as before', preceded by ':1360 a slow GPT verdict could keep the connection alive ~150s until the client's 120s axios timeout with no error event'. Prod flag state from baseline/railway-web-vars.txt and the container env dump.
findings.impact: The 'hard cap' is only hard up to the end of Phase 1; the verdict/critique/moderation tail rides free. Measured worst case is 103.7 s of a held connection on a single-worker single-loop server, which is 5x the median compare and long enough to be indistinguishable from a hang on the phone (the code comment names the client's 120 s axios timeout, so the user sees no error event at all - just a spinner). Twelve requests already exceeded 60 s. On a shared event loop each of these also occupies the process for its whole life, so one 103 s tail overlaps ~5 median compares.
findings.fix: Turn ENABLE_FULL_STREAM_DEADLINE ON (it is written, defaults OFF, and the docstring already prescribes 'Canary before flipping'), so the residual budget wraps the tail and expiry yields the best-available PARTIAL instead of an unbounded wait. findings.title: Prod runs in asia-southeast1 (Singapore) serving GCC users: measured 178 ms to Upstash and 131-884 ms to Supabase, while OpenAI and Serper are 3 ms away
findings.evidence: Container env: RAILWAY_REPLICA_REGION=asia-southeast1-eqsg3a. All 4,742 sampled HTTP requests carry edgeRegion=asia-southeast1-eqsg3a. Measured from inside the container: upstash whole-werewolf-125794.upstash.io median 178 ms; supabase qulajmyxdbdkchvecmvc.supabase.co median ~285 ms; TCP connect api.openai.com 2.6/2.9/3.0 ms, google.serper.dev 5.8/1.6/2.0 ms.
findings.repro: railway ssh -s web with scratchpad/m22-review/ls2/probe.py (read-only); railway logs --http --since 168h -s web --json | edgeRegion histogram (ls2/http168.json, n=4742).
findings.impact: The two dependencies on the request path that are NOT co-located are precisely the two that run inline on the event loop (finding 01). This reframes the fix: the 178/285 ms are not 'slow Redis' or 'slow Supabase', they are the price of a cross-region hop that is paid on every cache lookup and every log write. It also sets an upper bound on what offloading can buy - offloading removes the loop blockage but not the latency, so the specs/reviews cache-hit floor stays ~180 ms per lookup until the Upstash instance (and ideally the container) moves closer to the users and to each other. For GCC users this is compounded by the Singapore edge on the client side.
findings.fix: Two separable moves. (1) Cheap and immediate: co-locate Upstash and Supabase with the Railway region (or move the service to a region near both) so the 178/285 ms drop - this is a dashboard change, not a code change, and it is worth measuring before writing any code. (2) Reduce the number of hops: batch the per-product specs/reviews/price lookups into one Upstash pipeline call per product instead of one per stage, which turns 4-5 round trips per leg into 1. Re-run probe.py after each move; it is a 20-second read-only measurement.
findings.test_first: Not a unit test - a repeatable measurement: check probe.py into scripts/ as a read-only latency probe and assert in CI docs that Upstash p50 from the deploy region is under an agreed budget (say 40 ms) before launch.
findings.dedupe: new

findings.title: Prod emits zero per-request application logs (13 deploy log lines for 3.27 days and 4,742 requests) and Railway drops every log older than the current deployment
findings.evidence: railway logs --deployment --since 168h -s web returned 13 lines total: 9 startup + 4 auth warnings on 2026-09-05T17:33-34. Same window served 4,742 HTTP requests. findings.title: MAX_MONTHLY_COST=100 is set on BOTH prod services but the monthly budget guard is dead code with zero call sites, so nothing caps spend

An operator reading the Railway variables sees a $100/month spend cap and reasonably concludes spend is bounded; it is not bounded by anything. The live orchestrator tracks cost in self.total_cost and never routes it to the Redis meter, so both the counter and the gate are inert. At launch, with OpenAI credits restored, the first runaway loop has no ceiling. M13 flagged the symbols as dead code (P2, delete-them advice); the load-relevant fact is that the env var is SET in prod, which converts dead code into a misleading control.

findings.title: The container has an 8 vCPU / 8 GB quota but the start command runs one uvicorn worker with WEB_CONCURRENCY unset, so 7 of 8 cores are idle by construction
findings.evidence: Container cgroup (measured): cpu.max='800000 100000' => 8 vCPU quota; memory.max=8000000000 (8 GB), memory.current=166424576 (166 MB, 2.1%). Env: WEB_CONCURRENCY=<UNSET>, UVICORN_WORKERS=<UNSET>. railway.json startCommand 'uvicorn app.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port $PORT' and Procfile identical - no --workers, no --proxy-headers.
findings.repro: railway ssh -s web probe (cgroup reads + env dump, ls2/probe.out); git show 76ace90:railway.json; git show 76ace90:Procfile.
findings.impact: Every M18 conclusion that starts 'single event loop' is correct, but the reason is a missing flag, not a resource limit: the plan is paying for 8 vCPU and using ~1. The measured RSS is 166 MB, so 4 workers would fit in 8 GB with room to spare. This is the cheapest available capacity lever and it was not on the M18 list - though it is NOT free: the app keeps per-process state (the module-level Upstash client, the 40-thread executor, any in-process caches) and slowapi's limiter storage would become per-process unless it is backed by shared Redis, which is exactly the trap #72 describes. So this is a lever to evaluate deliberately, not to pull.
findings.fix: Before launch, evaluate --workers N (or WEB_CONCURRENCY) with N=2 as the first step, and gate it on two preconditions: (a) the slowapi limiter must use shared Upstash storage, not in-process (#72), otherwise N workers means N times the rate limit; (b) the executor is installed per process, so 40 threads becomes 40N - size it down accordingly. Add --proxy-headers at the same time (it is missing today and is needed for correct client IPs, which the limiter key work in #114 will depend on). Treat it as its own canary with the finding-05 overlap table as the acceptance measure.
findings.test_first: A startup test asserting that the limiter's storage_uri is a Redis URL and not in-process memory - red today - because that is the precondition that makes multi-worker safe.
findings.dedupe: new (M18 established single-loop/1-worker; the 8 vCPU quota, the 166 MB RSS headroom and the missing WEB_CONCURRENCY as the CAUSE are new)

findings.title: 44-50% of SUCCESSFUL comparisons per month record cost=0, so per-compare unit economics cannot be computed from the data the product collects
findings.evidence: Monthly: 2026-06 n=9,157 cost_sum $20.5276, cost==0 among successes 3,094 (44%); 2026-07 $2.1733, 1,223 (50%); 2026-08 $0.2890, 248 (46%). Cost histogram: 0.0 = 7,819 rows, 0.001 = 3,920 rows (one _track_serper_cost tick and nothing else). On the real subset only 3 of 1,501 successes are $0 - so the zeros are concentrated in the synthetic population plus short-circuit paths.
findings.repro: ls/MEASURED_NUMBERS.txt SECTION 4 (cost histogram + per-month cost==0 shares) and SECTION 13; independently re-derived totals in ls2/VERIFY.txt (cost_sum 22.9899 over the series; REAL successes 1,501 / $19.0699 / mean $0.0127).
findings.impact: Three separate mechanisms drive cost to zero - the failure paths (finding 04), the synthetic rows (finding 07), and genuine short-circuits (cache hits, category rejections) that legitimately spend ~nothing - and the schema cannot tell them apart, because 'this cost nothing' and 'we did not record what this cost' are the same value. The 3,920 rows at exactly $0.001 are the signature of a run that made one Serper call and stopped. Practical consequence: the mean of $0.0127 over real successes is the only defensible per-compare cost figure in the system, it rests on 1,501 rows all from June-July, and it is a floor for the two reasons in findings 03 and 04.
findings.fix: Make 'not measured' distinguishable from 'zero': write cost as NULL when the orchestrator produced no cost metadata and 0.0 only when it genuinely spent nothing, and add a small breakdown (gpt_calls, serper_calls, scrape_calls) to the row so a $0 can be audited. Combined with findings 03 and 04 this makes cost-per-compare a number the business can quote. Ship with the same migration that adds the `source` column from finding 07 so search_logs is altered once.
findings.test_first: A test asserting that a comparison which made zero API calls writes cost=0.0 while one whose metadata lacks total_cost writes NULL - red today (both write 0.0).
