ENABLE_SERPER_BREAKER is absent from railway-web-vars.txt for web and price-warmer, so _serper_breaker_enabled() is False, _serper_post short-circuits to _serper_post_impl unchanged, and _serper_record_failure returns before touching the breaker — the 403 branch at :449-450 is inert. SERPER_LIFETIME_LIMIT=0 on web makes _serper_gate_engaged() False (declared>0 required), so the budget gate admits every call too. This is exactly M13-32, shipped default-OFF; still dark. Two corrections. (1) measured_or_modelled should be MODELLED: repro2.py only shows 1 Serper POST + 1 BD POST via search_web; the ~14-18 POSTs/compare is arithmetic. (2) The 'every compare, forever' magnitude is contingent — prod sets both SERPER_API_KEY and SERPER_API_KEYS (values withheld). With >=2 resolved keys, _mark_serper_key_exhausted fires on the 403 and _active_serper_key() then returns None, short-circuiting later entry points BEFORE any POST; only the single-key INERT path dispatches every time. Fix and the arm-BD-gate-first ordering are correct. P2 matches M13-32.

Worst case per compare request is ~1x the resolver timeout, so the impact section's "10 x 22 s = 220 s of block per 60 s window" should read ~10 x 10-13 s = 100-130 s — still greater than the 60 s window, so the "permanent wedge from a single caller" conclusion survives unchanged. (2) The 11-12 s magnitude in the finding, and my own 13.50 s / 12.67 s through the real route with the REAL resolver, measure MY BOX, not Railway. I proved this box's resolver is pathological: `curl -w '%{time_namelookup}'` against the already-cached prod hostname gave namelookup 3.34 / 24.86 / 19.45 s (total 10.1 / 57.9 / 24.2 s, code=200 each time). Consequently every prod wall-clock probe I took (detect 32.5 s, 18.5 s, 13.3 s; health 12.9 s) is client-side noise and I discarded it — I can neither confirm nor refute prod-side magnitude from here. Railway-side ~10 s (glibc RES_TIMEOUT 5 x 2) stays MODELLED, and I agree with verifier 1 that the healthcheck-restart chain is UNPROVEN. P0 does not depend on either: the pathological host is fully attacker-supplied and unauthenticated, so the attacker picks the block duration by pointing url1 at a domain whose nameservers black-hole. (3) Line/route facts check out exactly: url_validator.py:30, url_routes.py:91/112/148/175/197/216, limiter keyed by get_remote_address at rate_limiter.py:52-58 with ENABLE_PROXY_AWARE_RATELIMIT off. DOES THE PROPOSED FIX CLOSE THE REPRO? Yes, measured. I ran the finder's exact proposal (`await asyncio.wait_for(asyncio.get_running_loop().getaddrinfo(host, None), timeout=2.0)` returning False on TimeoutError/gaierror) against the same 3 s stub: it returned False at 2.01 s with MAX_LOOP_GAP = **32 ms**, indistinguishable from the 31 ms idle baseline (assert gap <= 200 ms PASSES). So the loop-blocking defect is fully closed by the proposal. Verifier 1's caveat is still worth carrying but is MODELLED, not measured: `wait_for` cancels the await, not the libc call, so the worker thread stays occupied for the full ~10 s, and `loop.getaddrinfo` uses the default executor which main.py:168-171 bounds to 40 (app/utils/executor.py) shared with the ~33 to_thread adapter sites — 40 concurrent bogus URLs could starve that pool. My thread-count probe could NOT demonstrate this (active_count stayed 2 before and after the timeout) because httpx.ASGITransport does not run lifespan, so the bounded executor was never installed in my harness; treat "wait_for alone is sufficient" as unproven and size a dedicated resolver pool. IS test_first THE RIGHT RED TEST? Right shape — it is essentially what I built and it is genuinely red today (3000 ms gap vs a 200 ms assert) — but it has two defects as written. (a) `lambda *a, **k: time.sleep(3) or []` returns `[]`, so the IP loop finds nothing and validate_external_url returns **True**; the handler then falls through into `compare_from_urls` and does real network, making the test slow, network-dependent and flaky. Raise `socket.gaierror` after the sleep instead — the handler then short-circuits to a clean 400 with zero network (my run: status=400, body `{"success":false,"error":"URL blocked by security policy"...}`). (b) Because of the `or` short-circuit, do not assert "gap == 3 s x2"; assert a single max gap, or use url1-resolvable/url2-bogus to actually exercise two resolves. Also warm one request first and keep the threshold at 200 ms — idle heartbeat jitter on Windows measured 16-31 ms.
